title.zh: 卷四十八 志第二十九: 食貨三 錢幣
title.en: Volume 48 Treatises 29: Finance and Economics 3 - Money
title.raw: 卷四十八 志第二十九: 食貨三 錢幣 Volume 48 Treatises 29: Finance and Economics 3 - Money

sentences.zh: 錢幣。

translations.literal: Money and currency.
translations.idiomatic: Money and currency.

sentences.zh: 金初用遼、宋舊錢，天會末，雖劉豫「阜昌元寶」、「阜昌重寶」亦用之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jin, Liao and Song old coins were used; by the end of the Tianhui era, even Liu Yu's "Fuchang Yuanbao" and "Fuchang Chongbao" were also used.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Jin period the state used old Liao and Song coinage; by the end of the Tianhui reign even Liu Yu's Fuchang yuanbao and Fuchang chongbao were accepted.

sentences.zh: 海陵庶人貞元二年遷都之後，戶部尚書蔡松年複鈔引法，遂制交鈔，與錢並用。

translations.literal: After Prince Hailing moved the capital in the second year of Zhenyuan, Minister of Revenue Cai Songnian restored the note-circulation system, and exchange notes were instituted for use alongside coin.
translations.idiomatic: After Prince Hailing relocated the capital in Zhenyuan 2 (1154), Revenue Minister Cai Songnian revived the note-circulation system, and exchange notes were issued to circulate together with cash.

sentences.zh: 正隆二年，曆四十餘歲，始議鼓鑄。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenglong, after more than forty years had passed, coin casting was first discussed.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenglong 2 (1157), more than forty years after the founding of the dynasty, the court first debated instituting official coinage.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，初禁銅越外界，懸罪賞格。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, copper was first forbidden to be taken beyond the borders, with posted penalties and reward scales.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that winter the state first barred the export of copper beyond the frontier and posted statutory penalties and rewards.

sentences.zh: 括民間銅鍮器，陝西、南京者輸京兆，他路悉輸中都。

translations.literal: Bronze and brass vessels among the people were requisitioned; those in Shaanxi and Nanjing circuit were delivered to Jingzhao, and all other circuits delivered theirs to the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Household bronze and brass ware was seized: items from Shaanxi and Nanjing circuits went to Jingzhao, while every other circuit sent its haul to the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，中都置錢監二，東曰寶源，西曰寶豐。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year, two mints were established in the Central Capital—the eastern called Baoyuan and the western Baofeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year three (1158) two mints were set up at the Central Capital, Baoyuan in the east and Baofeng in the west.

sentences.zh: 京兆置監一。

translations.literal: One mint was established at Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: A single mint was also established at Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 曰利用。

translations.literal: It was called Liyong.
translations.idiomatic: It was named Liyong.

sentences.zh: 三監鑄錢，文曰「正隆通寶」，輕重如宋小平錢，而肉好字文峻整過之，與舊錢通用。

translations.literal: The three mints cast coin inscribed "Zhenglong Tongbao," of weight like the Song small standard cash, yet with rim, hole, and characters more sharply finished than the old coins, and they circulated together with the old money.
translations.idiomatic: All three mints cast Zhenglong Tongbao cash, matching the Song small-denomination standard in weight but with sharper rims, square holes, and lettering; the new pieces circulated alongside older coin.

sentences.zh: 世宗大定元年，用吏部尚書張中彥言，命陝西路參用宋舊鐵錢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dading under Emperor Shizong, following the advice of Minister of Personnel Zhang Zhongyan, the Shaanxi Circuit was ordered to use Song old iron cash concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 1 (1161), at Minister of Personnel Zhang Zhongyan's recommendation, Emperor Shizong ordered the Shaanxi Circuit to accept Song iron cash alongside other currency.

sentences.zh: 四年，浸不行，詔陝西行戶部、並兩路通檢官，詳究其事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year it gradually ceased to be implemented; an edict ordered the Shaanxi Circuit Revenue Office and the circuit-wide inspection commissioners of both routes to investigate the matter in detail.
translations.idiomatic: By the fourth year the policy had largely lapsed; the throne ordered the Shaanxi revenue office and the circuit inspection commissioners on both routes to investigate.

sentences.zh: 皆言：「民間用錢，名與鐵錢兼用，其實不為准數，公私不便。

translations.literal: All said: "Among the people, cash is nominally used together with iron money, but in fact it does not serve as a standard measure, and both public and private affairs are inconvenient."
translations.idiomatic: They all reported that although cash and iron coin were supposed to circulate together, in practice no reliable standard held and both government and populace found the arrangement unworkable.

sentences.zh: 」遂罷之。

translations.literal: " The policy was then abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The measure was therefore withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 八年，民有犯銅禁者，上曰：「銷錢作銅，舊有禁令。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when the people violated the copper prohibition, the emperor said: "Melting coin to make copper goods—there has long been a ban on this."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, after subjects breached the copper ban, the emperor remarked, "Turning coin into copper wares has been forbidden for generations."

sentences.zh: 然民間猶有鑄鏡者，非銷錢而何？

translations.literal: Yet among the people there are still those who cast mirrors—if not from melted coin, then from what?
translations.idiomatic: Yet people still cast bronze mirrors—where else would the metal come from if not melted coin?

sentences.zh: 」遂並禁之。

translations.literal: " Both were then forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore banned mirror-casting as well.

sentences.zh: 十年，上諭戶部臣曰：「官錢積而不散，則民間錢重，貿易必艱，宜令市金銀及諸物。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the emperor instructed the Revenue Ministry officials: "When government cash accumulates without being released, cash among the people becomes scarce and trade must grow difficult; you should order the purchase of gold, silver, and various goods."
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he told revenue officials, "When the treasury hoards coin, private cash grows scarce and commerce stalls—buy gold, silver, and other commodities to draw money back into circulation."

sentences.zh: 其諸路酤榷之貨，亦令以物平折輸之。

translations.literal: For monopoly goods on the various circuits, they were also ordered to accept payment in kind at fair conversion rates.
translations.idiomatic: Monopoly goods on the circuits were likewise to be collected in kind at fair assessed values.

sentences.zh: 」十月，上責戶部官曰：「先以官錢率多，恐民間不得流通，令諸處貿易金銀絲帛，以圖流轉。

translations.literal: " In the tenth month, the emperor reproached the Revenue officials: "Earlier, because government cash was excessively abundant and we feared the people could not circulate it, we ordered various places to trade in gold, silver, and silk to promote circulation."
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he rebuked them: "We had ordered markets to trade gold, silver, and silk because the treasury held too much coin and private circulation was stifled."

sentences.zh: 今知乃有以抑配反害百姓者。

translations.literal: Now we learn that there are those who, through forced allocation, instead harm the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Now we find that forced quotas have ended up harming the people instead.

sentences.zh: 前許院務得折納輕齎之物以便民，是皆朕思而後行者也，此尚出朕，安用若為。

translations.literal: Previously we permitted the palace workshops to accept light, portable goods in commutation to benefit the people—these were all measures I considered before enacting; even these still came from me—of what use are you?
translations.idiomatic: I myself authorized the palace workshops to accept portable goods in lieu of cash to ease burdens on the people—policies I devised before issuing—and you still botch them. What need is there for officials like you?

sentences.zh: 又隨處時有賑濟，往往近地無糧，取於它處，往返既遠，人愈難之。

translations.literal: Moreover, relief is frequently dispensed in various places, yet often there is no grain nearby and it must be taken from elsewhere; with the journey back and forth so long, the people find it ever harder.
translations.idiomatic: Relief is handed out everywhere, yet nearby districts often lack grain and must draw supplies from afar; the long haul only adds to popular hardship.

sentences.zh: 何為不隨處起倉。

translations.literal: Why not establish granaries in each place?
translations.idiomatic: Why not build granaries locally in every region?

sentences.zh: 年豐則多糴以備賑贍，設有緩急，亦豈不易辦乎？

translations.literal: In years of abundance, buy more grain to prepare for relief and support; if there is an emergency, would it not be easy to manage?
translations.idiomatic: In good harvest years you could buy extra grain for relief stores, so that when crisis comes supplies would be close at hand.

sentences.zh: 而徒使錢充府庫，將安用之。

translations.literal: Yet you merely let coin fill the government treasuries—what use will that be?
translations.idiomatic: Instead you merely let coin pile up in the treasury—what good does that do?

sentences.zh: 天下之大，朕豈能一一遍知，凡此數事，汝等何為而使至此。

translations.literal: The realm is vast—how could I know every matter one by one? For all these several affairs, what have you done to bring things to this pass?
translations.idiomatic: The empire is vast and I cannot know every detail myself—how did you officials let these several abuses reach this point?

sentences.zh: 且戶部與它部不同，當從宜為計，若但務因循，以守其職，則戶部官誰不能為。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Revenue Ministry differs from other ministries—it must plan according to circumstances; if you merely cling to routine to guard your posts, then who cannot serve as a Revenue official?
translations.idiomatic: The Revenue Ministry is not like other departments—it must adapt policy to circumstances. Anyone can hold the post if all you do is cling to precedent.

sentences.zh: 」十一年二月，禁私鑄銅鏡。

translations.literal: " In the second month of the eleventh year, private casting of bronze mirrors was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eleventh year private mirror-casting was banned.

sentences.zh: 舊有銅器悉送官，給其直之半。

translations.literal: All existing copper vessels were to be delivered to the government, and half their value was paid.
translations.idiomatic: Householders had to surrender existing copper ware to the state, receiving half its appraised value in return.

sentences.zh: 惟神佛像、鐘、磬、鈸、鈷、腰束帶、魚袋之屬，則存之。

translations.literal: Only divine and Buddha images, bells, chime-stones, cymbals, ritual staffs, waist girdles, fish pouches, and the like were permitted to remain.
translations.idiomatic: Only religious images, temple bells and chimes, cymbals, ritual implements, official belt fittings, and fish pouches were exempted.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月，以銅少，命尚書省遣使諸路規措銅貨。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twelfth year, because copper was scarce, the Imperial Secretariat was ordered to dispatch envoys on the various circuits to arrange copper supplies.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twelfth year, with copper in short supply, the Secretariat sent envoys to every circuit to procure metal.

sentences.zh: 能指坑冶得實者，賞。

translations.literal: Those who could identify mines and smelters that proved genuine were rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Informants who located workable mines and smelters received rewards.

sentences.zh: 上與宰臣議鼓鑄之術，宰臣曰：「有言所在有金銀坑冶，皆可采以鑄錢，臣竊謂工費過於所得數倍，恐不可行。

translations.literal: The emperor discussed coin-casting methods with his chief ministers; the ministers said: "Some say that wherever there are gold and silver mines they can all be mined to cast coin; your servant privately considers that labor costs exceed the yield several times over and fears it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: Discussing minting policy with his ministers, they replied, "Some propose mining every gold and silver deposit to cast coin, but labor costs would exceed output several times over—we doubt it is feasible."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「金銀，山澤之利，當以與民，惟錢不當私鑄。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Gold and silver are the bounty of mountains and marshes and should be given to the people; only coin must not be privately cast."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered, "Gold and silver are natural resources that should benefit the people; only coin must never be privately cast."

sentences.zh: 今國家財用豐盈，若流布四方與在官何異？

translations.literal: Now the state's revenues are abundant—if they circulate throughout the realm, how does that differ from remaining in government hands?
translations.idiomatic: The treasury is flush today—if wealth spreads through the realm, how is that different from hoarding it in government coffers?

sentences.zh: 所費雖多，但在民間，而新錢日增爾。

translations.literal: The expense may be great, but it remains among the people, and new coin increases daily.
translations.idiomatic: Costs may be high, yet the money stays among the people and fresh coinage grows day by day.

sentences.zh: 其遣能吏經營之。

translations.literal: Dispatch capable officials to manage it.
translations.idiomatic: Send capable administrators to oversee the work.

sentences.zh: 」左丞石琚進曰：「臣聞天子之富藏在天下，錢貨如泉，正欲流通。

translations.literal: " Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Shi Jue advanced and said: "Your servant has heard that the Son of Heaven's wealth lies stored throughout the realm; money and goods are like a spring—the very point is to let them flow."
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Censor Shi Jue added, "A ruler's wealth lies with the people; currency should flow like a spring—that is the whole purpose."

sentences.zh: 」上複問琚曰：「古亦有民自鑄錢者乎？

translations.literal: " The emperor again asked Jue: "In antiquity, did the people also cast coin themselves?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked again, "Did commoners ever cast their own coin in antiquity?"

sentences.zh: 」琚對曰：「民若自鑄，則小人圖利，錢益薄惡，此古所以禁也。

translations.literal: " Jue replied: "If the people cast coin themselves, petty men will seek profit and the coin grows ever thinner and baser—this is why antiquity forbade it."
translations.idiomatic: Jue answered, "If subjects minted their own coin, schemers would debased it for profit—that is why antiquity banned private casting."

sentences.zh: 」十三年，命非屯兵之州府，以錢市易金帛，運致京師，使錢幣流通，以濟民用。

translations.literal: " In the thirteenth year, prefectures and districts without garrison troops were ordered to use coin to purchase silk and cloth and transport them to the capital so that currency would circulate and supply the people's needs.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year non-garrison prefectures were told to buy silk and cloth with coin and ship the goods to the capital, keeping currency moving to meet popular needs.

sentences.zh: 十五年十一月，上謂宰臣曰：「或言鑄錢無益，所得不償所費。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fifteenth year, the emperor said to his chief ministers: "Some say casting coin is useless and the yield does not repay the cost."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fifteenth year he told his ministers, "Some claim minting is pointless because costs exceed returns."

sentences.zh: 朕謂不然。

translations.literal: I say it is not so.
translations.idiomatic: I disagree.

sentences.zh: 天下如一家，何公私之間，公家之費私家得之，但新幣日增，公私俱便也。

translations.literal: The realm is like one household—what distinction between public and private? Public expenditure becomes private gain, yet new coin increases daily and both public and private benefit.
translations.idiomatic: The empire is one household—why split public and private? Treasury spending becomes popular income as new coin multiplies, benefiting state and people alike.

sentences.zh: 」十六年三月，遣使分路訪察銅礦苗脈。

translations.literal: " In the third month of the sixteenth year, envoys were dispatched on separate routes to investigate copper ore deposits.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the sixteenth year envoys were sent on each circuit to survey copper veins.

sentences.zh: 十八年，代州立監鑄錢，命震武軍節度使李天吉、知保德軍事高季孫往監之，而所鑄斑駁黑澀不可用，詔削天吉、季孫等官兩階，解職，仍杖季孫八十。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, a mint was established in Daizhou to cast coin; Military Commissioner of Zhenwu Army Li Tianji and Supervisor of Baode Army Affairs Gao Jisun were ordered to supervise it, but the coin cast was mottled, dark, and rough and could not be used; an edict reduced Tianji, Jisun, and others two ranks in office, removed them from their posts, and still flogged Jisun eighty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Daizhou gained a mint supervised by Li Tianji of Zhenwu command and Gao Jisun of Baode command, but their coin came out blotchy, dark, and unusable; both men were demoted two ranks and dismissed, and Jisun was flogged eighty strokes.

sentences.zh: 更命工部郎中張大節、吏部員外郎麻珪監鑄。

translations.literal: Zhang Dajie, Director in the Ministry of Works, and Ma Gui, Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel, were then appointed to supervise the casting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dajie of the Works Bureau and Ma Gui of the Personnel Bureau were reassigned to oversee minting.

sentences.zh: 其錢文曰「大定通寶」，字文肉好又勝正隆之制，世傳其錢料微用銀雲。

translations.literal: The coin was inscribed "Dading Tongbao"; its characters, rim, and hole again surpassed the Zhenglong standard, and the world reports that its alloy used a trace of silver.
translations.idiomatic: The new cash bore the legend Dading Tongbao, with sharper characters and rims than the Zhenglong issue; tradition holds that the alloy contained a trace of silver.

sentences.zh: 十九年，始鑄至萬六千餘貫。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, casting first reached more than sixteen thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: By the nineteenth year output reached just over sixteen thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 二十年，詔先以五千進呈，而後命與舊錢並用。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, an edict ordered that five thousand strings first be presented, and only afterward were they commanded to circulate together with old coin.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year five thousand strings were presented for inspection before the court authorized circulation alongside older coin.

sentences.zh: 初，新錢之未行也，以宋大觀錢作當五用之。

translations.literal: At first, before the new coin was issued, Song Daguan cash was used at a rate of five to one.
translations.idiomatic: Before the new coin circulated, Song Daguan pieces were accepted at a five-for-one valuation.

sentences.zh: 二月，上聞上京修內所，市民物不即與直，又用短錢，責宰臣曰：「如此小事，朕豈能悉知？

translations.literal: In the second month, the emperor heard that at the Shangjing Palace Workshops, when buying goods from the market they did not promptly pay fair price and also used short strings of cash; he reproached the chief ministers: "On such minor matters, how can I know everything?"
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he learned that Shangjing palace workshops haggled over market purchases and paid in short strings; he scolded his ministers, "How can I know every petty abuse myself?"

sentences.zh: 卿等何為不察也。

translations.literal: Why do you not investigate?
translations.idiomatic: Why were you not watching for this?

sentences.zh: 」時民間以八十為陌，謂之短錢，官用足陌，謂之長錢。

translations.literal: " At the time the people used eighty cash per string, called short money; the government used full strings of one hundred, called long money.
translations.idiomatic: Private trade counted only eighty cash per string—"short money"—while official accounts used full hundreds, called "long money."

sentences.zh: 大名男子斡魯補者上言，謂官私所用錢皆當以八十為陌，遂為定制。

translations.literal: A man of Daming named Wolu Bu memorialized that both public and private cash should all use eighty per string, and this became the fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: A Daming commoner named Wolu Bu petitioned that government and private accounts alike should adopt the eighty-cash string, and the rule became permanent law.

sentences.zh: 二十年十一月，名代州監曰阜通，設監一員，正五品，以州節度兼領。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the twentieth year, the Daizhou mint was named Futong; one superintendent was established, rank 5a, concurrently held by the circuit military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the twentieth year the Daizhou mint was renamed Futong, with a rank-5a superintendent post held concurrently by the circuit commissioner.

sentences.zh: 副監一員，正六品，以州同知兼領。

translations.literal: One vice superintendent, rank 6a, concurrently held by the prefectural vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: A rank-6a vice superintendent was added, filled by the prefectural vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 丞一員，正七品，以觀察判官兼領。

translations.literal: One assistant, rank 7a, concurrently held by the surveillance circuit judge.
translations.idiomatic: A rank-7a assistant post went to the circuit surveillance judge.

sentences.zh: 設勾當官二員，從八品。

translations.literal: Two handling officials of rank 8b were established.
translations.idiomatic: Two rank-8b handling clerks were also appointed.

sentences.zh: 給銀牌，命副監及丞更馳驛經理。

translations.literal: Silver tallies were issued, and the vice superintendent and assistant were ordered to take turns traveling by courier post to manage affairs.
translations.idiomatic: They received silver courier tallies and rotated duty traveling the post roads to manage operations.

sentences.zh: 二十二年十月，以參加政事粘割斡特剌提控代州阜通監。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the twenty-second year, Participating Administrator Nianzha Gwatela was assigned to supervise the Daizhou Futong Mint.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the twenty-second year Participating Administrator Nianzha Gwatela was placed in charge of the Daizhou Futong mint.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，上以阜通監鼓鑄歲久，而錢不加多，蓋以代州長貳廳幕兼領，而奪於州務，不得專意綜理故也。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, the emperor said that although the Futong Mint had cast coin for many years, the amount did not increase—likely because Daizhou's chief and secondary officials and clerks held it concurrently and were absorbed in prefectural affairs, unable to devote themselves wholly to overall management.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he noted that despite years of operation Futong output had not grown, because prefectural leaders and staff held the posts concurrently and were distracted by routine administration.

sentences.zh: 遂設副監、監丞為正員，而以節度領監事。

translations.literal: Vice superintendent and mint assistant were then made regular posts, while the military commissioner retained nominal supervision.
translations.idiomatic: Vice superintendent and assistant became full-time posts, with the military commissioner retaining nominal oversight.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，上曰：「中外皆言錢難，朕嘗計之，京師積錢五百萬貫亦不為多，外路雖有終亦無用，諸路官錢非屯兵處可盡運至京師。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, the emperor said: "Within and without all say cash is scarce; I have reckoned that even five million strings accumulated in the capital is not much; though the outer circuits have cash, in the end it is useless—official cash on the circuits where there are no garrison troops can all be transported to the capital."
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he remarked, "Everyone complains of scarce cash, yet five million strings in the capital is not excessive; coin hoarded on distant circuits does no good—treasury cash from non-garrison districts should all be shipped to the capital."

sentences.zh: 」太慰丞相克甯曰：「民間錢固已艱得，若盡歸京師，民益艱得矣！

translations.literal: " Grand Preceptor and Chancellor Kening said: "Cash among the people is already hard to obtain; if it all returns to the capital, the people will find it even harder!"
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Kening objected, "Cash is already scarce among the people—draining the provinces would only make matters worse!"

sentences.zh: 不若起其半至都，餘半變折輕齎，則中外皆便。

translations.literal: Better to move half to the capital and convert the other half into light, portable goods—then both capital and circuits will benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Better to move half to the capital and convert the rest into portable goods, benefiting court and countryside alike.

sentences.zh: 」十一月，上諭宰臣曰：「國家銅禁久矣，尚聞民私造腰帶及鏡，托為舊物，公然市之，宜加禁約。

translations.literal: " In the eleventh month, the emperor instructed the chief ministers: "The state's copper ban has long been in force, yet we still hear that the people privately make belts and mirrors, passing them off as old goods and openly selling them—this should be further restricted."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he told his ministers, "Despite the long-standing copper ban, people still forge belts and mirrors, disguise them as antiques, and sell them openly—tighten enforcement."

sentences.zh: 」二十七年二月，曲陽縣鑄錢別為一監，以利通為名，設副監、監丞，給驛更出經營銅事。

translations.literal: " In the second month of the twenty-seventh year, coin casting in Quyang County was made a separate mint named Litong; vice superintendent and assistant were established, courier posts were provided, and they took turns going out to manage copper affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twenty-seventh year Quyang County gained its own Litong mint with full-time deputies who rotated along the post roads to procure copper.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，上謂宰臣曰：「今者外路見錢其數甚多，聞有六千餘萬貫，皆在僻處積貯。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, the emperor said to his chief ministers: "Nowadays cash on the outer circuits is very great in number—we hear there are more than sixty million strings, all stored in remote places.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he told his ministers, "Cash on the circuits is enormous—some sixty million strings sit idle in remote storehouses.

sentences.zh: 既不流散，公私無益，與無等爾。

translations.literal: Since it neither circulates nor benefits public or private affairs, it is the same as having none.
translations.idiomatic: Because it never circulates, it helps neither state nor people—it might as well not exist.

sentences.zh: 今中都歲費三百萬貫，支用不繼，若致之京師，不過少有挽運之費，縱所費多，亦惟散在民爾。

translations.literal: Now the Central Capital spends three million strings yearly and cannot keep up; if it is brought to the capital, there would be only a little transport cost—even if the expense is great, it would still merely be dispersed among the people.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Capital spends three million strings a year and still runs short; shipping the hoard here would cost little in transport, and even heavy expense would only spread wealth among the populace.

sentences.zh: 」章宗大定二十九年十二月，雁門、五台民劉完等訴：「自立監鑄錢以來，有銅礦之地雖曰官運，其顧直不足則令民共償。

translations.literal: " In the twelfth month of the twenty-ninth year of Dading under Emperor Zhangzong, the people Liu Wan and others of Yanmen and Wutai petitioned: "Since the mints were established to cast coin, in places with copper mines although transport is called official, when the hired wages are insufficient the people are made to share the cost."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Dading 29 (1189) Liu Wan and others of Yanmen and Wutai petitioned Emperor Zhangzong: "Since the mints opened, districts with copper mines must cover shortfalls in official transport wages."

sentences.zh: 乞與本州司縣均為差配。

translations.literal: We beg that it be apportioned equally with the prefecture and county offices of this circuit.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that levies be shared equally among prefectural and county offices.

sentences.zh: 」遂命甄官署丞丁用楫往審其利病，還言：「所運銅礦，民以物力科差濟之，非所願也。

translations.literal: " Selection Office Assistant Director Ding Yongji was then sent to examine the benefits and harms; on his return he said: "For the copper ore transported, the people supply it through labor-service assessments of material resources—not willingly."
translations.idiomatic: Selection Office aide Ding Yongji was dispatched to investigate and reported that households supplied transport through corvée assessments against their property, not voluntarily.

sentences.zh: 其顧直即低，又有刻剝之弊。

translations.literal: The hired wages are moreover low, and there is also the abuse of extortion.
translations.idiomatic: Official wages were low to begin with, and officials extorted more on top.

sentences.zh: 而相視苗脈工匠，妄指人之垣屋及寺觀謂當開採，因以取賄。

translations.literal: The craftsmen who surveyed ore veins falsely identified people's walls and temple compounds as sites to be mined and thereby took bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Survey crews falsely marked private walls and monasteries for mining and took bribes.

sentences.zh: 又隨冶夫匠，日辦淨銅四兩，多不及數，複銷銅器及舊錢，送官以足之。

translations.literal: Moreover, smelting artisans were required daily to furnish four ounces of refined copper, often falling short; they again melted copper vessels and old coin and delivered them to the government to make up the quota.
translations.idiomatic: Smelters owed four ounces of refined copper daily, often fell short, and melted household ware and old coin to meet quotas.

sentences.zh: 今阜通，利通兩監，歲鑄錢十四萬餘貫，而歲所費乃至八十餘萬貫，病民而多費，未見其利便也。

translations.literal: Now the two mints Futong and Litong cast more than one hundred forty thousand strings yearly, yet yearly costs reach more than eight hundred thousand strings—harming the people with heavy expense, and no benefit is seen.
translations.idiomatic: Futong and Litong together mint about 140,000 strings a year while costing over 800,000—burdening the people without clear benefit.

sentences.zh: 」宰臣以聞，遂罷代州、曲陽二監。

translations.literal: " The chief ministers reported this, and the two mints of Daizhou and Quyang were then abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers relayed the findings and the Daizhou and Quyang mints were abolished.

sentences.zh: 初，貞元間既行鈔引法，遂設印造鈔引庫及交鈔庫，皆設使、副、判各一員，都監二員，而交鈔庫副則專主書押、搭印合同之事。

translations.literal: At first, after the note-circulation system was implemented in the Zhenyuan era, the Note Printing Treasury and the Exchange Note Treasury were established; each had one commissioner, vice commissioner, and reviewer, and two chief inspectors, while the vice commissioner of the Exchange Note Treasury specialized in countersigning, affixing seals, and contract matters.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhenyuan note system began, the court created the Note Printing Treasury and Exchange Note Treasury, each headed by a commissioner, deputy, and reviewer plus two inspectors; the exchange deputy handled countersignatures and seal contracts.

sentences.zh: 印一貫、二貫、三貫、五貫、十貫五等，謂之大鈔；

translations.literal: Notes of one, two, three, five, and ten strings were printed—these were called large notes;
translations.idiomatic: Large notes were printed in denominations of one, two, three, five, and ten strings;

sentences.zh: 一百、二百、三百、五百、七百五等，謂之小鈔。

translations.literal: one hundred, two hundred, three hundred, five hundred, and seven hundred cash in five grades were called small notes.
translations.idiomatic: small notes came in five grades of one hundred, two hundred, three hundred, five hundred, and seven hundred cash.

sentences.zh: 與錢並行，以七年為限，納舊易新。

translations.literal: They circulated together with coin, with a term of seven years, old notes surrendered for new.
translations.idiomatic: They circulated with coin on a seven-year cycle of exchange for new notes.

sentences.zh: 猶循宋張詠四川交子之法而紓其期爾，蓋亦以銅少，權制之法也。

translations.literal: It still followed the Song method of Zhang Yong's Sichuan exchange notes while easing the term—likely also because copper was scarce, a provisional expedient.
translations.idiomatic: The system followed Song Zhang Yong's Sichuan jiaozi model with a longer redemption period—a stopgap born of copper scarcity.

sentences.zh: 時有欲罷之者，至是二監既罷，有司言：「交鈔舊同見錢，商旅利於致遠，往往以錢買鈔，蓋公私俱便之事，豈可罷去！

translations.literal: At the time some wished to abolish them; now that the two mints had been abolished, the responsible offices said: "Exchange notes were formerly equivalent to ready cash; merchants and travelers benefit for long-distance transport and often buy notes with coin—this is convenient for both public and private—how can it be abolished!"
translations.idiomatic: Some had wanted to abolish notes altogether; after the mints closed officials argued that notes equaled ready cash, eased long-distance trade, and benefited everyone— they must not be scrapped.

sentences.zh: 止因有厘革年限，不能無疑，乞削七年厘革之法，令民得常用。

translations.literal: It is only because there is a term for renewal that doubts cannot be avoided; we beg to abolish the seven-year renewal law so the people may use them regularly.
translations.idiomatic: Only the seven-year renewal cycle breeds distrust; abolish it so people can rely on notes indefinitely.

sentences.zh: 若歲久字文磨滅，許於所在官庫納舊換新，或聽便支錢。

translations.literal: If after many years the characters are worn away, surrender of old notes for new at the local government treasury is permitted, or cash may be drawn at convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Worn notes may be exchanged at local treasuries or cashed out on demand.

sentences.zh: 」遂罷七年厘革之限，交鈔字昏方換。

translations.literal: " The seven-year renewal limit was then abolished; exchange notes were replaced only when the characters grew illegible.
translations.idiomatic: The seven-year renewal rule was dropped; notes were replaced only when the text faded.

sentences.zh: 法自此始，而收斂無術，出多入少，民浸輕之。

translations.literal: From this the law began, yet there was no method of recall; more was issued than taken in, and the people gradually held them cheap.
translations.idiomatic: From this reform onward the state lacked recall discipline, issued more than it redeemed, and popular confidence eroded.

sentences.zh: 厥後其法屢更，而不能革，弊亦始於此焉。

translations.literal: Thereafter the law was changed many times yet could not be reformed—the abuses also began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Later statutes changed repeatedly without fixing the problem; the chronic abuses trace to this decision.

sentences.zh: 交鈔之制，外為闌，作花紋，其上衡書貫例，左曰：「某字料。

translations.literal: In the exchange-note system, the outer border bore decorative patterns; across the top the string denomination was written in balance; on the left it read: "Such-and-such character batch."
translations.idiomatic: Exchange notes had a decorative border; the denomination ran across the top, with the left margin reading "Batch [character]."

sentences.zh: 」右曰：「某字型大小。

translations.literal: " On the right it read: "Such-and-such character, size large or small."
translations.idiomatic: The right margin read "[Character], size large/small."

sentences.zh: 」料號外，篆書曰：「偽造交鈔者斬，告捕者賞錢三百貫。

translations.literal: " Outside the batch number, in seal script it read: "Those who forge exchange notes are beheaded; informants who capture them are rewarded three hundred strings of cash."
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the batch number seal script warned, "Forgers of exchange notes face execution; informants receive three hundred strings."

sentences.zh: 」料號衡闌下曰：「中都交鈔庫，准尚書戶部符，承都堂劄付，戶部覆點勘，令史姓名押字。

translations.literal: " Below the batch number and horizontal border it read: "Central Capital Exchange Note Treasury, pursuant to the Imperial Secretariat Revenue Ministry tally, receiving the Council Chancery directive, Revenue Ministry re-inspection and tally, clerk's name and seal."
translations.idiomatic: Below the batch line: "Central Capital Exchange Note Treasury, per Revenue Ministry authorization, per Council directive, Revenue re-audit, clerk signature."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「聖旨印造逐路交鈔，於某處庫納錢換鈔，更許於某處庫納鈔換錢，官私同見錢流轉。

translations.literal: " It also read: "By imperial order, exchange notes for each circuit are printed; at such-and-such treasury coin is paid to obtain notes, and again at such-and-such treasury notes are paid to obtain coin—public and private alike circulate like ready cash."
translations.idiomatic: It also stated: "By imperial order circuit notes are printed; specified treasuries exchange coin for notes and notes for coin, circulating like ready cash for public and private use."

sentences.zh: 」其鈔不限年月行用，如字文故暗，鈔紙擦磨，許于所屬庫司納舊換新。

translations.literal: " The notes were not limited by year or month for use; if the characters were worn dark or the paper rubbed thin, surrender of old for new at the responsible treasury was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Notes had no expiry; faded text or worn paper could be exchanged at the responsible treasury.

sentences.zh: 若到庫支錢，或倒換新鈔，每貫克工墨錢若干文。

translations.literal: If cash was drawn at the treasury or new notes exchanged, a certain number of cash per string was deducted for labor and ink costs.
translations.idiomatic: Cashing out or swapping for new notes incurred a per-string labor and ink fee.

sentences.zh: 庫掐、攢司、庫副、副使、使各押字，年月日。

translations.literal: The treasury clerk, collection clerk, vice superintendent, vice commissioner, and commissioner each affixed their seals, with year, month, and day.
translations.idiomatic: Treasury clerks, collectors, deputies, and commissioners each signed with the date.

sentences.zh: 印造鈔引庫庫子、庫司、副使各押字，上至尚書戶部官亦押字。

translations.literal: The Note Printing Treasury attendants, clerks, and vice commissioners each affixed seals, up to the Imperial Secretariat Revenue officials who also affixed seals.
translations.idiomatic: Note Printing Treasury staff signed in turn, up to Revenue Ministry officials in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 其搭印支錢處合同，餘用印依常例。

translations.literal: At places where disbursement of cash required combined seals, officials jointly sealed; for other use of seals, follow the usual practice.
translations.idiomatic: Where cash disbursement required combined seals, officials co-signed together; all other seal usage followed standing procedure.

sentences.zh: 初，大定間定制，民間應許存留銅鍮器物，若申賣入官，每斤給錢二百文。

translations.literal: At first, during the Dading period regulations were established: copper and brass vessels among the people were permitted to be retained—if reported and sold to the government, two hundred cash per jin was paid.
translations.idiomatic: Under early Dading rules the people might keep copper and brass wares; voluntary sale to the state paid two hundred cash per jin.

sentences.zh: 其{去廾}藏應禁器物，首納者每斤給錢百文，非器物銅貨一百五十文，不及斤者計給之。

translations.literal: For privately hoarded prohibited vessels, those who first surrendered them received one hundred cash per jin; for non-vessel copper goods, one hundred fifty cash; for amounts under one jin, payment was calculated proportionally.
translations.idiomatic: Private hoarders of banned metalware who came forward first received one hundred cash per jin, or one hundred fifty for loose copper; amounts under one jin were paid by weight.

sentences.zh: 在都官局及外路造賣銅器價，令運司佐貳檢校，鏡每斤三百十四文，鍍金禦仙花腰帶十七貫六百七十一文，五子荔支腰帶十七貫九百七十一文，抬鈒羅文束帶八貫五百六十文，魚袋二貫三百九文，鈸鈷鐃磬每斤一貫九百二文，鈴杵坐銅者二貫七百六十九文，鍮石者三貫六百四十六文。

translations.literal: Prices for copper vessels manufactured and sold at the capital bureaus and outer-circuit offices were ordered inspected by transport commission deputies: mirrors three hundred fourteen cash per jin, gilded Imperial Immortal Flower waist belts seventeen strings six hundred seventy-one cash, Five Sons Lychee waist belts seventeen strings nine hundred seventy-one cash, embossed luo-pattern cincture belts eight strings five hundred sixty cash, fish pouches two strings three hundred nine cash, cymbals, gongs, chimes, and bells one string nine hundred two cash per jin, bell-stand bronze two strings seven hundred sixty-nine cash, bell-stand brass three strings six hundred forty-six cash.
translations.idiomatic: Transport deputies were to verify prices for state-made copperware in the capital and provinces: mirrors at 314 cash per jin; gilded Imperial Immortal Flower belts at 17,671 strings; Five Sons Lychee belts at 17,971; embossed cinctures at 8,560; fish pouches at 2,309; cymbals and bells at 1,902 per jin; bronze bell-stands at 2,769; brass bell-stands at 3,646.

sentences.zh: 明昌二年十月，敕減賣鏡價，防私鑄銷錢也。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Mingchang, an edict reduced mirror sale prices, to guard against private casting and melting coin.
translations.idiomatic: In Mingchang 2 (1191), tenth month, mirror prices were cut to deter illicit minting and coin-smelting.

sentences.zh: 舊嘗以夫匠逾天山北界外采銅，明昌三年，監察御史李炳言：「頃聞有司奏，在官銅數可支十年，若複每歲令夫匠過界遠采，不惟多費，複恐或生邊釁。

translations.literal: Formerly corvée artisans had been sent beyond the northern border outside the Tianshan to mine copper. In the third year of Mingchang, Supervising Censor Li Bing said: "I recently heard officials report that official copper stores could supply ten years. If corvée artisans were again sent across the border each year for distant mining, not only would expense multiply—I also fear it could provoke border incidents.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée miners had long crossed north of the Tianshan for copper. In Mingchang 3 (1192) Censor Li Bing warned: "Official stores can last a decade—annual border expeditions waste money and risk frontier friction.

sentences.zh: 若支用將盡之日，止可於界內采煉。

translations.literal: When the day of exhaustion draws near, mining and smelting should be confined within the border only.
translations.idiomatic: Only when supplies ran low should mining be limited to within the border.

sentences.zh: 」上是其言，遂不許出界。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved his words and thereupon forbade going beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and banned cross-border mining.

sentences.zh: 五月，敕尚書省曰：「民間流轉交鈔，當限其數，毋令多於見錢也。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, an edict to the Imperial Secretariat said: "Exchange notes circulating among the people should be limited in number—let them not exceed ready cash."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Secretariat was ordered to cap note circulation so it would not exceed hard cash.

sentences.zh: 」四年，上諭宰臣曰：「隨處有無用官物，可為計置，如鐵錢之類是也。

translations.literal: " In the fourth year, the emperor instructed the chief ministers: "Wherever there are useless government goods, plans may be devised to utilize them—iron cash is such a case."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he told his ministers to repurpose idle state goods, citing iron cash as an example.

sentences.zh: 」或有言鐵錢有破損，當令所司以銅錢償之者，參知政事胥持國不可，上曰：「令償之尚壞，不償將盡壞矣！

translations.literal: Someone said that damaged iron cash should be replaced with copper cash by the responsible office; Vice Grand Councilor Xu Chiguo objected. The emperor said: "If we mandate replacement they may still be damaged; if we do not replace them they will be utterly ruined!
translations.idiomatic: When an official proposed redeeming damaged iron cash with copper, Xu Chiguo demurred. The emperor replied: "Paying replacements they may still break; refuse payment and none will survive!

sentences.zh: 若果無用，曷別為計？

translations.literal: If they are truly useless, why not devise another plan?
translations.idiomatic: If iron cash is truly worthless, find another use for it.

sentences.zh: 」持國曰：「如江南用銅錢，江北、淮南用鐵錢，蓋以隔閡銅錢不令過界爾。

translations.literal: Xu Chiguo said: "As south of the Yangzi uses copper cash while north of the river and Huainan use iron cash—this is precisely to block copper cash from crossing the boundary.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Chiguo explained: "Jiangnan uses copper while the north and Huainan use iron expressly to keep copper from crossing regional lines.

sentences.zh: 如陝西市易亦有用銀布姜麻，若舊有鐵錢，宜姑收貯，以備緩急。

translations.literal: In Shaanxi markets silver, cloth, ginger, and hemp are also used in trade; if iron cash already exists, it is fitting for the time being to collect and store it against emergencies."
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi also trades in silver, cloth, ginger, and hemp—existing iron cash should be stockpiled for emergencies."

sentences.zh: 」遂令有司籍鐵錢及諸無用之物，貯於庫。

translations.literal: Thereupon officials were ordered to register iron cash and various useless items and store them in treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were told to inventory iron cash and other idle goods for storage.

sentences.zh: 八月，提刑司言：「所降陝西交鈔多於見錢，使民艱於流轉。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the Judicial Inspection Commission said: "Exchange notes issued in Shaanxi exceed ready cash, making circulation difficult for the people."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Judicial Commission reported that Shaanxi notes outnumbered cash, stifling trade.

sentences.zh: 」宰臣以聞，遂令本路榷稅及諸名色錢，折交鈔。

translations.literal: The chief ministers reported this; thereupon Shaanxi monopoly taxes and assorted named fees were ordered converted to exchange notes.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers relayed the complaint; Shaanxi excise and miscellaneous fees were made payable in notes.

sentences.zh: 官兵俸，許錢絹銀鈔各半之，若錢銀數少，即全給交鈔。

translations.literal: Military and civilian salaries were permitted to be half cash, silk, silver, and notes; if cash and silver were insufficient in quantity, full payment in exchange notes was given.
translations.idiomatic: Salaries could be half cash, silk, silver, and notes; shortages of coin and silver were met fully in paper.

sentences.zh: 五年三月，宰臣奏：「民間錢所以艱得，以官豪家多積故也。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year, the chief ministers memorialized: "The reason cash is hard to obtain among the people is that officials and powerful households hoard heavily."
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year ministers blamed scarce cash on hoarding by officials and rich households.

sentences.zh: 在唐元和間，嘗限富家錢過五千貫者死，王公重貶沒入，以五之一賞告者。

translations.literal: Under the Tang Yuanhe period, wealthy families holding more than five thousand strings faced death; princes and high nobles faced heavy penalties and confiscation; one-fifth was rewarded to informants.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yuanhe law had executed families hoarding over 5,000 strings, punished great clans with confiscation, and paid informants one-fifth of the seizure.

sentences.zh: 」上令參酌定制，令官民之家以品從物力限見錢，多不過二萬貫，猛安謀克則以牛具為差，不得過萬貫，凡有所餘，盡令易諸物收貯之。

translations.literal: " The emperor ordered a considered regulation established: official and private households, by rank and property assessment, were limited in ready cash—no more than twenty thousand strings; chiefs and company commanders by ox-plough quota, no more than ten thousand strings; all surplus was ordered converted into goods and stored.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor drafted limits by rank and wealth: officials and commoners might keep up to 20,000 strings; chiefs and company officers up to 10,000; surplus had to be invested in goods.

sentences.zh: 有能告數外留錢者，奴婢免為良，傭者出離，以十之一為賞，餘皆沒入。

translations.literal: Those able to report cash retained beyond the limit—the slave was freed to commoner status, hired laborers were released; one-tenth was given as reward, the remainder all confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Informants on illegal hoarding won slaves their freedom, freed hired workers, took one-tenth of the hoard as reward, and forfeited the rest.

sentences.zh: 又諭旨有司，凡使高麗還者，所得銅器令盡買之。

translations.literal: The emperor also instructed officials: all returning from Goryeo missions were ordered to sell all copper vessels obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys returning from Goryeo were required to sell any copperware they had acquired.

sentences.zh: 承安二年十月，宰臣奏：「舊立交鈔法，凡以舊易新者，每貫取工墨錢十五文。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Chengan, the chief ministers memorialized: "Under the old exchange-note law, whenever old notes were exchanged for new, fifteen cash in labor-and-ink fees was taken per string."
translations.idiomatic: Chengan 2 (1197), tenth month: ministers noted that renewing old notes had cost fifteen cash per string in labor and ink fees.

sentences.zh: 至大定二十三年，不拘貫例，每張收八文，既無益於官，亦妨鈔法，宜從舊制便。

translations.literal: By the twenty-third year of Dading, regardless of string denomination, eight cash per note was collected—it benefited the government nothing and also hindered the note system; it is fitting to return to the old system."
translations.idiomatic: Since Dading 23 (1183) the fee had been a flat eight cash per note, helping neither treasury nor circulation—they urged a return to the old rule.

sentences.zh: 若以鈔買鹽引，每貫權作一貫五十文，庶得多售。

translations.literal: If notes are used to purchase salt certificates, each string may temporarily count as one string fifty cash, so that more may be sold."
translations.idiomatic: They also proposed valuing each note string at 1.05 strings when buying salt certificates to boost sales.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「工墨錢，貫可令收十二文。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "For labor-and-ink fees, twelve cash per string may be collected."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor set the renewal fee at twelve cash per string.

sentences.zh: 買鹽引者，每貫可權作一貫一百文。

translations.literal: For those purchasing salt certificates, each string may temporarily count as one string one hundred cash.
translations.idiomatic: Salt-certificate purchases would credit each string at 1.1 strings.

sentences.zh: 」時交鈔所出數多，民間成貫例者艱於流轉，詔以西北二京、遼東路從宜給小鈔，且許於官庫換錢，與它路通行。

translations.literal: " At that time the number of exchange notes issued was great; whole-string denominations among the people were difficult to circulate; an edict ordered the Northwest Two Capitals and Liaodong Circuit to issue small notes as appropriate, and permitted exchange for cash at government treasuries, valid on other circuits as well.
translations.idiomatic: With heavy note issuance making large denominations unwieldy, the Northwest capitals and Liaodong were allowed to issue small notes redeemable at treasuries for use nationwide.

sentences.zh: 十二月，尚書省議，謂時所給官兵俸及邊戍軍須，皆以銀鈔相兼，舊例銀每鋌五十兩，其直百貫，民間或有截鑿之者，其價亦隨低昂，遂改鑄銀名「承安寶貨」，一兩至十兩分五等，每兩折錢二貫，公私同見錢用，仍定銷鑄及接受稽留罪賞格。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the Imperial Secretariat deliberated, stating that military and frontier salaries then paid were partly in silver and notes under the old rule—a silver ingot of fifty taels, its value one hundred strings; among the people some cut and chiseled them, and the price also rose and fell—thereupon recast silver was named "Chengan Treasure Goods," from one tael to ten taels in five grades, each tael exchangeable for two strings of cash, for public and private use like ready cash; penalties and rewards for melting, casting, and detention were also fixed.
translations.idiomatic: That December the Secretariat noted that salary silver came in fifty-tael ingots worth 100 strings—often chipped by traders. They recoined Chengan Treasure silver in five denominations from one to ten taels, two strings per tael, usable like cash, with penalties for illicit smelting or hoarding.

sentences.zh: 承安三年正月，省奏：「隨處榷場若許見錢越境，雖非銷毀，即與銷毀無異。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Chengan, the ministry memorialized: "If ready cash is permitted to cross borders at monopoly markets everywhere, though it is not melting, it is no different from melting."
translations.idiomatic: Chengan 3 (1198), first month: the ministry warned that letting cash cross border markets was tantamount to export smelting.

sentences.zh: 」遂立制，以錢與外方人使及與交易者，徒五年，三斤以上死，駔儈同罪。

translations.literal: " A regulation was then established: giving cash to foreign envoys or in trade—five years penal servitude; three jin or more, death; brokers same offense.
translations.idiomatic: Cash given to foreign envoys or used in cross-border trade drew five years' penal servitude, death for amounts over three jin; brokers faced the same penalties.

sentences.zh: 捕告人之賞，官先為代給錢五百貫。

translations.literal: Reward for capturing and reporting: the government first advanced five hundred strings of cash on the informant's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Informants received five hundred strings upfront from the state.

sentences.zh: 其逮及與接引、館伴，先排、通引、書表等以次坐罪，仍令均償。

translations.literal: Those arrested and those who received, escorted, preceded, guided, or drafted documents were punished in descending order of responsibility, and were also ordered to share compensation equally.
translations.idiomatic: Escorts, guides, clerks, and others involved were punished in descending order and made to share restitution.

sentences.zh: 時交鈔稍滯，命西京、北京、臨潢，遼東等路一貫以上俱用銀鈔、寶貨，不許用錢，一貫以下聽民便。

translations.literal: At the time exchange notes were somewhat stagnant; orders were issued that in the Western Capital, Northern Capital, Linhuang, Liaodong, and other circuits, amounts of one string and above must all use silver notes and treasure goods—cash not permitted; below one string the people might choose as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: To ease note stagnation, the western and northern capitals and Liaodong required silver notes or treasure goods for payments of one string and above; smaller sums remained at choice.

sentences.zh: 時既行限錢法，人多不遵，上曰：「已定條約，不為不重，其令御史台及提刑司察之。

translations.literal: At the time the cash-limit law was already in force, yet many people did not comply. The emperor said: "The regulations already fixed are not unduly lenient—the Censorate and Judicial Commissions are ordered to investigate."
translations.idiomatic: Despite strict cash-hoarding limits, compliance was poor; the emperor ordered the Censorate and Judicial Commissions to enforce them.

sentences.zh: 」九月，以民間鈔滯，盡以一貫以下交鈔易錢用之，遂複減元限之數，更定官民存留錢法，三分為率，親王、公主、品官許留一分，餘皆半之，其贏餘之數期五十日內盡易諸物，違者以違制論，以錢賞告者。

translations.literal: " In the ninth month, because notes stagnated among the people, all exchange notes of one string and below were exchanged for cash for use; the original limits were then further reduced; the law on cash retention by officials and private persons was revised—using one-third as the standard: princes, princesses, and ranked officials were permitted to retain one share, the rest half that; surplus beyond the quota was to be fully converted into goods within fifty days—violators prosecuted as violating regulations; cash rewarded to informants.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month small notes were cashed out and hoarding limits tightened to one-third of prior quotas—princes and ranked officials kept one share, others half; surplus had to be invested within fifty days or face penalties, with cash rewards for informants.

sentences.zh: 於兩行部各置回易務，以綿絹物段易銀鈔，亦許本務納銀鈔。

translations.literal: Exchange bureaus were placed in both Route Headquarters to exchange silk and cloth goods for silver notes, and payment in silver notes at the bureau itself was also permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Route headquarters opened exchange offices trading silk and cloth for silver notes and accepting note payments.

sentences.zh: 赴榷貨出鹽引，納鈔于山東、河北、河東等路，從便易錢。

translations.literal: Salt certificates issued by the Monopoly Office—notes paid in Shandong, Hebei, Hedong, and other circuits might be exchanged for cash at convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Salt certificates could be bought with notes and cashed at choice in Shandong, Hebei, Hedong, and allied circuits.

sentences.zh: 各降補官及德號空敕三百、度牒一千，從兩行部指定處，限四月進納補換。

translations.literal: Three hundred supplementary appointment commissions and one thousand ordination certificates with honorary titles but empty credentials were distributed; at designated places under both Route Headquarters, submission and exchange were limited to the fourth month.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred honorary appointments and one thousand blank ordination certificates were offered for redemption at designated route offices by the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 又更造一百例小鈔，並許官庫易錢。

translations.literal: One-hundred-denomination small notes were also newly made, and exchange for cash at government treasuries was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: New small notes in 100-string denominations were issued, redeemable at treasuries.

sentences.zh: 一貫、二貫例並支小鈔，三貫例則支銀一兩、小鈔一貫，若五貫、十貫例則四分支小鈔、六分支銀，欲得寶貨者聽，有阻滯及輒減價者罪之。

translations.literal: For one- and two-string denominations small notes were disbursed entirely; for three-string denominations one tael of silver and one string in small notes; for five- and ten-string denominations forty percent in small notes and sixty percent in silver—those wishing treasure goods were permitted; obstruction or arbitrary price reduction was criminalized.
translations.idiomatic: Payments of one or two strings came in small notes; three-string payments split one tael silver plus one string in notes; five- and ten-string payments were 40% notes and 60% silver—or treasure goods on request—with penalties for obstruction or discounting.

sentences.zh: 四年三月，又以銀鈔阻滯，乃權止山東諸路以銀鈔與綿絹鹽引從便易錢之制。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year, because silver notes were stagnant, the temporary measure allowing silver notes, silk, and salt certificates to be exchanged for cash at convenience in Shandong and other circuits was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Chengan 4, third month: flexible note-to-cash exchange in Shandong was suspended amid silver-note stagnation.

sentences.zh: 令院務諸科名錢，除京師、河南、陝西銀鈔從便，余路並許收銀鈔各半，仍於鈔四分之一許納其本路。

translations.literal: Named fees at government wine shops and various categories—except in the capital, Henan, and Shaanxi where silver notes were at choice—in all other circuits half payment in silver notes was permitted, and of the note payment one-quarter might be paid in notes of the local circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Wine-shop and other official fees—except in the capital, Henan, and Shaanxi—could be half paid in silver notes, one-quarter of which might be local-circuit notes.

sentences.zh: 隨路所收交鈔，除本路者不復支發，余通行者並迴圈用之。

translations.literal: Exchange notes collected on each circuit—with the exception of notes of the local circuit, which were not reissued—those circulating from elsewhere were all recirculated for use.
translations.idiomatic: Notes collected locally were not reissued; notes from other circuits were recycled back into circulation.

sentences.zh: 榷貨所鬻鹽引，收納寶貨與鈔相半，銀每兩止折鈔兩貫。

translations.literal: Salt certificates sold by the Monopoly Office accepted treasure goods and notes in equal shares; each tael of silver exchanged for only two strings of notes.
translations.idiomatic: Salt certificates required half payment in treasure goods and half in notes, with silver valued at only two strings per tael.

sentences.zh: 省許人依舊詣庫納鈔，隨路漕司所收，除額外羨餘者，亦如之。

translations.literal: The ministry permitted people to pay notes at treasuries as before; for collections by transport commissions on each circuit, surplus beyond the quota was treated likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Treasuries still accepted note deposits; transport surplus above quotas followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 所支官錢，亦以銀鈔相兼，銀已零截者令交鈔庫不復支，若寶貨數少，可浸增鑄。

translations.literal: Official disbursements likewise combined silver and notes; fragmented silver was ordered not to be disbursed again by the exchange-note treasuries; if treasure goods were insufficient in number, casting might gradually be increased.
translations.idiomatic: Official payouts mixed silver and notes; chipped silver was no longer issued from note treasuries; more treasure goods might be cast if supplies ran low.

sentences.zh: 銀鈔既通則物價自平，雖有禁法亦安所施、遂除阻滯銀鈔罪制。

translations.literal: Once silver and notes circulated freely, prices would naturally stabilize—even if prohibition laws existed, where could they be applied? Thereupon the penalties for obstructing silver notes were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: With free circulation prices would stabilize without need for coercion—penalties for hoarding silver notes were lifted.

sentences.zh: 四年，以戶部言，命在都官錢、榷貨務鹽引，並聽收寶貨，附近鹽司貼錢數亦許帶納。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, on the Revenue Ministry's petition, orders were issued that capital official cash and salt certificates at the Monopoly Office might all accept treasure goods; nearby salt offices' supplemental cash payments were also permitted to include them in payment.
translations.idiomatic: Chengan 4: at ministerial request, capital treasuries and monopoly salt offices were ordered to accept treasure goods, including supplemental salt fees.

sentences.zh: 民間寶貨有所歸，自然通行，不至銷毀。

translations.literal: Among the people treasure goods had a destination; they naturally circulated and would not be melted down.
translations.idiomatic: With official outlets for treasure goods, private stock would circulate rather than be melted.

sentences.zh: 先是，設四庫印小鈔以代鈔本，令人便齎小鈔赴庫換錢，即與支見錢無異。

translations.literal: Previously, four treasuries printed small notes in place of note backing, permitting people conveniently to carry small notes to treasuries to exchange for cash—no different from disbursing ready cash.
translations.idiomatic: Four treasuries had issued small notes backed by reserves, letting people redeem them for cash on demand like hard coin.

sentences.zh: 今更不須印造，俟其換盡，可罷四庫。

translations.literal: Now printing is no longer required; when they are exhausted through exchange, the four treasuries may be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Printing would cease; once existing small notes were redeemed out, the four treasuries could close.

sentences.zh: 但以大鈔驗錢數支易見錢。

translations.literal: Only large notes verifying the cash amount would be used to disburse and exchange ready cash.
translations.idiomatic: Large-denomination notes alone would back cash disbursement.

sentences.zh: 時私鑄「承安寶貨」者多雜以銅錫，浸不能行，京師閉肆。

translations.literal: At the time private casting of "Chengan Treasure Goods" often adulterated them with copper and tin; they gradually could not circulate, and shops in the capital closed.
translations.idiomatic: Counterfeit Chengan treasure alloyed with copper and tin drove the currency from markets until capital shops shut their doors.

sentences.zh: 五年十二月，宰奏臣：「比以軍儲調發，支出交鈔數多。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fifth year, the chief ministers memorialized: "Recently because military stores were deployed and dispatched, the amount of exchange notes disbursed was great."
translations.idiomatic: Chengan 5 (1200), twelfth month: ministers reported heavy note issuance to fund military deployments.

sentences.zh: 遂鑄寶貨，與錢兼用，以代鈔本，蓋權時之制，非經久之法。

translations.literal: Thereupon treasure goods were cast for concurrent use with cash, to replace note backing—it was a temporary measure, not a lasting law."
translations.idiomatic: Treasure goods had been coined alongside cash as a temporary substitute for note reserves—not a permanent fix.

sentences.zh: 」遂罷「承安寶貨」。

translations.literal: " Thereupon "Chengan Treasure Goods" were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Chengan treasure was abolished.

sentences.zh: 泰和元年六月，通州刺史盧構言：「民間鈔固已流行，獨銀價未平，官之所定每鋌以十萬為准，而市肆才直八萬，蓋出多入少故也。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Taihe, Tongzhou Prefect Lu Gou said: "Exchange notes among the people already circulate freely; only silver prices are not stable—the government sets each ingot at one hundred thousand as standard, yet markets value them at only eighty thousand, because output exceeds intake."
translations.idiomatic: Taihe 1 (1201), sixth month: Tongzhou Prefect Lu Gou noted that while notes circulated, silver traded at 80,000 against an official 100,000 per ingot because supply outran demand.

sentences.zh: 若令諸稅以錢銀鈔三分均納。

translations.literal: If all taxes are required to pay one-third each in cash, silver, and notes.
translations.idiomatic: Require taxes to be paid one-third each in cash, silver, and notes.

sentences.zh: 庶革其弊。

translations.literal: Perhaps this would reform the abuses."
translations.idiomatic: That might balance the market."

sentences.zh: 」下省議，宰臣謂：「軍興以來，全賴交鈔佐用，以出多遂滯，頃令院務收鈔七分，亦漸流通。

translations.literal: " It was referred to the ministry for deliberation; the chief ministers said: "Since the rise of warfare, reliance has been entirely on exchange notes to supplement use; because output was great they stagnated; recently government wine shops were ordered to accept notes at seventy percent—they are gradually circulating again.
translations.idiomatic: Referred to ministry debate, ministers replied that wartime finance depended on notes; though oversupply had stalled them, requiring wine shops to take 70% notes was restoring circulation.

sentences.zh: 若與銀均納，則彼增此減，理必偏勝，至礙鈔法。

translations.literal: If payment were equalized with silver, one would increase as the other decreased—by reason one side would necessarily prevail, and ultimately the note system would be obstructed."
translations.idiomatic: Equal silver shares would cannibalize note demand and undermine paper currency.

sentences.zh: 必欲銀價之平，宜令諸名若'鋪馬'、'軍須'等錢，許納銀半，無者聽便。

translations.literal: If silver prices must be stabilized, it is fitting to order various named fees such as "relay-horse" and "military supplies" and the like to permit half payment in silver—where none is available, convenience is permitted."
translations.idiomatic: To stabilize silver, named levies such as relay-horse and military-supply fees should accept half payment in silver where available.

sentences.zh: 」先是，嘗行三合同交鈔，至泰和二年，止行於民間，而官不收斂，朝廷慮其病民，遂令諸稅各帶納一分，雖止系本路者，亦許不限路分通納。

translations.literal: " Previously, triple-contract exchange notes had been issued; by the second year of Taihe they circulated only among the people while the government did not collect them—the court feared this harmed the people and thereupon ordered each tax to include one-tenth payment; even those confined to the local circuit were permitted unrestricted cross-circuit payment."
translations.idiomatic: Triple-contract notes had circulated only privately until Taihe 2 (1202), when the court required one-tenth of all taxes—even local levies—to be paid in them, acceptable nationwide.

sentences.zh: 戶部見征累年鋪馬錢，亦聽收其半。

translations.literal: The Revenue Ministry, collecting relay-horse fees accumulated over years, also permitted collection of half in them.
translations.idiomatic: The Revenue Ministry also allowed half of accumulated relay-horse fees to be paid in these notes.

sentences.zh: 閏十二月，上以交鈔事，召戶部尚書孫鐸、侍郎張複亨，議於內殿。

translations.literal: In the intercalary twelfth month, the emperor, on exchange-note affairs, summoned Revenue Minister Sun Duo and Vice Minister Zhang Fuheng to deliberate in the inner hall.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalary twelfth month: the emperor summoned Revenue Minister Sun Duo and Vice Minister Zhang Fuheng to discuss note policy in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 複亨以三合同鈔可行，鐸請廢不用，既而複亨言竟詘。

translations.literal: Fuheng held that triple-contract notes could be implemented; Duo requested abolition and no use—thereupon Fuheng's proposal was ultimately rejected.
translations.idiomatic: Fuheng favored triple-contract notes; Duo wanted them scrapped—and Duo prevailed.

sentences.zh: 自是而後，國虛民貧，經用不足，專以交鈔愚百姓，而法又不常，世宗之業衰焉。

translations.literal: From this time onward the state was empty and the people poor; routine expenditures were insufficient; they relied exclusively on exchange notes to mislead the common people—and the laws were not constant; the enterprise of Emperor Shizong declined.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter fiscal exhaustion and erratic note policy eroded Shizong's legacy as the state leaned on paper money to the people's detriment.

sentences.zh: 以至泰和三年，其弊彌甚，乃謂宰臣曰：「大定間，錢至足，今民間錢少，而又不在官，何耶？

translations.literal: By the third year of Taihe the abuses grew ever worse; he said to the chief ministers: "During the Dading period cash was abundant—now among the people cash is scarce, yet it is not in government hands—why?"
translations.idiomatic: By Taihe 3 (1203) he asked his ministers why Dading-era coin abundance had given way to private hoarding with empty public coffers.

sentences.zh: 其集問百官，必有能知之者。

translations.literal: Let officials be assembled and questioned—the knowledgeable must surely be among them."
translations.idiomatic: Summon the bureaucracy—someone must know the cause."

sentences.zh: 」四年七月，罷限錢法，從戶部尚書上官瑜所請也。

translations.literal: " In the seventh month of the fourth year, the cash-limit law was abolished, on the petition of Revenue Minister Shangguan Yu."
translations.idiomatic: Taihe 4 (1204), seventh month: cash hoarding limits were lifted at Revenue Minister Shangguan Yu's request.

sentences.zh: 四年，欲增鑄錢，命百官議所以足銅之術。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, wishing to increase coin casting, the emperor ordered the hundred officials to deliberate on means to secure sufficient copper.
translations.idiomatic: That year, planning expanded minting, he ordered officials to propose ways to secure copper.

sentences.zh: 中丞孟鑄謂：「銷錢作銅，及盜用出境者不止，宜罪其官及鄰。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Meng Zhu said: "Melting coin to make copper and illicit use by export beyond the border do not cease—it is fitting to punish the official and neighbors."
translations.idiomatic: Censor Meng Zhu urged punishing local officials and neighbors for coin-smelting and copper smuggling.

sentences.zh: 」太府監梁絪等言：「鑄錢甚費，率費十錢可得一錢。

translations.literal: " Director of the Palace Storehouse Liang Yin and others said: "Coin casting is extremely costly—generally ten cash spent yields one cash."
translations.idiomatic: Palace Storehouse Director Liang Yin reported minting cost ten cash for every one produced.

sentences.zh: 識者謂費雖多猶增一錢也，乞采銅、拘器以鑄。

translations.literal: Those who understood the matter said that though the expense was great, it still added one cash; they requested copper mining and seizure of vessels for casting."
translations.idiomatic: Advisors argued the cost still netted one cash per coin and urged mining and confiscating vessels for bronze.

sentences.zh: 」宰臣謂：「鼓鑄未可速行，其銅治聽民煎煉，官為買之。

translations.literal: " The chief ministers said: "Hasty coin casting cannot be undertaken; copper smelting is permitted among the people—the government will purchase it.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers replied minting could wait but the state would buy privately smelted copper.

sentences.zh: 凡寺觀不及十人，不許畜法器。

translations.literal: Monasteries and temples with fewer than ten persons were not permitted to keep ritual vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Temples with fewer than ten residents could not retain ritual bronze.

sentences.zh: 民間鍮銅器期 以兩月送官給價。

translations.literal: Among the people, brass and copper vessels were to be delivered to the government within two months for fixed payment.
translations.idiomatic: Household brass and copper had to be surrendered within two months for official payment.

sentences.zh: 匿者以私法坐，限外人告者，以知而不糾坐其官。

translations.literal: Concealers were prosecuted under private law; where outsiders reported, officials were punished for knowing and not investigating.
translations.idiomatic: Concealment brought criminal penalties; officials who failed to act on outside reports shared guilt.

sentences.zh: 寺觀許童行告者賞。

translations.literal: Monasteries and temples were permitted to reward juvenile acolytes who reported.
translations.idiomatic: Temples might reward novice informants.

sentences.zh: 俟銅多，別具以聞。

translations.literal: When copper is plentiful, a separate memorial will be submitted."
translations.idiomatic: Further minting plans would follow once copper stockpiles grew."

sentences.zh: 」八月，定從便易錢法，聽人輸納于京師，而于山東、河北、大名、河東等路依數支取。

translations.literal: " In the eighth month, the flexible cash-exchange law was fixed: people were permitted to pay in at the capital and draw the amount in Shandong, Hebei, Daming, Hedong, and other circuits according to quota.
translations.idiomatic: August: a flexible remittance law let people deposit at the capital and draw cash in Shandong, Hebei, Daming, Hedong, and allied regions.

sentences.zh: 後鑄大錢一直十，篆文曰「泰和重寶」，與鈔參行。

translations.literal: Later large coins worth ten standard cash each were cast, seal script reading "Taihe Heavy Treasure," circulating together with notes.
translations.idiomatic: Later the court issued Taihe chongbao heavy coins worth ten cash each, circulating alongside paper.

sentences.zh: 五年，上欲罷交鈔工墨錢，複以印時常費遂命貫止收六文。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the emperor wished to abolish exchange-note labor-and-ink fees, but because printing entailed constant expense, an order was issued that no more than six cash per string would be collected.
translations.idiomatic: Taihe 5: he nearly abolished note renewal fees but settled on six cash per string given printing costs.

sentences.zh: 六年四月，陝西交鈔不行，以見錢十萬貫為鈔本，與鈔相易，複以小鈔十萬貫相參用之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the sixth year, Shaanxi exchange notes did not circulate; one hundred thousand strings of ready cash were set as note backing, exchanged for notes, and one hundred thousand strings in small notes were again used in combination.
translations.idiomatic: Taihe 6 (1206), fourth month: Shaanxi notes failed; the state backed them with 100,000 strings cash plus 100,000 in small notes.

sentences.zh: 六年十一月，複許諸路各行小鈔。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the sixth year, each circuit was again permitted to issue small notes separately.
translations.idiomatic: Taihe 6, eleventh month: circuits regained authority to issue local small notes.

sentences.zh: 中都路則於中都及保州，南京路則于南京、歸德、河南府，山東東路則於益都、濟南府，山東西路則于東平、大名府，河北東路則於河間府、冀州，河北西路則於真定、彰德府，河東南路則於平陽，河東北路則於太原、汾州，遼東則於上京、咸平，西京則於西京、撫州，北京則於臨潢府官庫易錢。

translations.literal: The Central Capital Route exchanged at the Central Capital and Baozhou; the Southern Capital Route at the Southern Capital, Guide, and Henan Prefecture; Shandong Eastern Route at Yidu and Jinan Prefecture; Shandong Western Route at Dongping and Daming Prefecture; Hebei Eastern Route at Hejian Prefecture and Jizhou; Hebei Western Route at Zhending and Zhangde Prefecture; Hedong Southern Route at Pingyang; Hedong Northern Route at Taiyuan and Fenzhou; Liaodong at Upper Capital and Xianping; Western Capital at Western Capital and Fuzhou; Northern Capital at Linhuang Prefecture government treasuries—for cash exchange.
translations.idiomatic: Each circuit redeemed notes at designated treasuries: the Central Capital route at the capital and Baozhou; the Southern Capital route at Nanjing, Guide, and Henan; Shandong east at Yidu and Jinan; Shandong west at Dongping and Daming; Hebei east at Hejian and Jizhou; Hebei west at Zhending and Zhangde; southern Hedong at Pingyang; northern Hedong at Taiyuan and Fenzhou; Liaodong at the Upper Capital and Xianping; the Western Capital at Fuzhou; the Northern Capital at Linhuang.

sentences.zh: 令戶部印小鈔五等，附各路同見錢用。

translations.literal: Orders were issued that the Revenue Ministry print small notes in five denominations, for use alongside ready cash on each circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Revenue Ministry issued five denominations of small notes for circuit-wide use with cash.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，敕在官毋得支出大鈔，在民者令赴庫，以多寡制數易小鈔及見錢，院務商稅及諸名錢，三分須納大鈔一分，惟遼東以便。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year, an edict forbade government offices from disbursing large notes; among the people, those holding them were ordered to go to treasuries and exchange by quantity into small notes and ready cash; wine-shop commercial taxes and assorted named fees required one-third payment in large notes—except Liaodong, for convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Taihe 7 (1207), first month: offices could not pay out large notes; holders had to redeem them for small notes or cash; a third of wine-shop and commercial fees had to be paid in large notes—Liaodong excepted.

sentences.zh: 時民以貨幣屢變，往往怨嗟，聚語於市。

translations.literal: At the time, because currency changed repeatedly, the people often complained and gathered to talk in markets.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated currency changes bred market grumbling and public gatherings.

sentences.zh: 上知之，諭旨于御史台曰：「自今都市敢有相聚論鈔法難行者，許人捕告，賞錢三百貫。

translations.literal: The emperor learned of this and instructed the Censorate: "From now on, if in the capital markets anyone dares gather to discuss difficulties in the note system, capture and report is permitted—a reward of three hundred strings of cash."
translations.idiomatic: He told the Censorate to reward three hundred strings for reporting groups discussing note policy in the capital.

sentences.zh: 」五月，以戶部尚書高汝礪議，立「鈔法條約」，添印大小鈔，以鈔庫至急切，增副使一員。

translations.literal: " In the fifth month, on Revenue Minister Gao Ruli's proposal, the "Note System Covenant" was established; large and small notes were added to printing; because the note treasuries were extremely pressed, one additional vice commissioner was added.
translations.idiomatic: May: Minister Gao Ruli's Note System Covenant expanded printing and added a deputy commissioner to overstretched note treasuries.

sentences.zh: 汝礪又與中都路轉運使孫鐸言錢幣，上命中丞孟鑄、禮部侍郎喬宇、國子司業劉昂等十人議，月餘不決。

translations.literal: Ruli also discussed currency with Central Capital Transport Commissioner Sun Duo; the emperor ordered Vice Censor-in-Chief Meng Zhu, Ritual Vice Minister Qiao Yu, National University Vice Director Liu Ang, and ten others to deliberate—for more than a month without decision.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ruli debated currency with transport chief Sun Duo; ten officials including Meng Zhu, Qiao Yu, and Liu Ang debated for over a month without agreement.

sentences.zh: 七月，上召議於泰和殿，且諭汝礪曰：「今後毋謂鈔多，不加重而輒易之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, the emperor summoned them to deliberate in the Taihe Hall, and also instructed Ruli: "From now on do not, because notes are numerous, fail to add weight and rashly change them.
translations.idiomatic: July he convened them at Taihe Hall and warned Gao Ruli not to swap note issues merely because circulation was heavy.

sentences.zh: 重之加于錢，可也。

translations.literal: Adding weight relative to cash—that is acceptable."
translations.idiomatic: He might add nominal weight against cash—but not replace denominations lightly."

sentences.zh: 」明日，敕：「民間之交易、典質、一貫以上並用交鈔，毋得用錢。

translations.literal: " The next day, an edict: "Among the people, in trade, pawn, and transactions of one string and above, exchange notes must be used—cash must not be used.
translations.idiomatic: Next day an edict required notes for private trade and pawn of one string or more; cash was banned.

sentences.zh: 須立契者，三分之一用諸物。

translations.literal: Where contracts must be established, one-third may be in various goods.
translations.idiomatic: Written contracts might value one-third of the payment in goods.

sentences.zh: 六盤山西、遼河東以五分之一用鈔，東鄙屯田戶以六分之一用鈔。

translations.literal: West of Liupan Mountain and east of the Liao River, one-fifth in notes; eastern frontier garrison colonists, one-sixth in notes.
translations.idiomatic: West of Liupan and east of the Liao, one-fifth of transactions had to be in notes; eastern garrison colonists paid one-sixth.

sentences.zh: 不須立契者，惟遼東錢鈔從便。

translations.literal: Where no contract is required, only in Liaodong may cash and notes be at convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Informal transactions remained free to use cash or notes only in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 犯者徒二年，告者賞有差，監臨犯者杖且解職，縣官能奉行流通者升除，否者降罰，集眾沮法者以違制論。

translations.literal: Violators sentenced to two years penal servitude; informers rewarded in graded amounts; supervising officials who violate receive beating and dismissal from office; county officials who can implement and circulate [notes] are promoted and appointed; otherwise demoted and punished; those who gather crowds to obstruct the law are prosecuted as violations of imperial orders.
translations.idiomatic: Violators faced two years' penal servitude, with graded rewards for informers. Supervising officials who broke the rules were beaten and stripped of office. County officials who kept notes circulating were promoted; those who failed were demoted and fined. Anyone who rallied crowds to sabotage the system was charged with violating imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 工墨錢每張止收二錢。

translations.literal: Processing-and-ink fees per sheet limited to two cash coins.
translations.idiomatic: Processing fees were capped at two cash per note.

sentences.zh: 商旅齎見錢不得過十貫。

translations.literal: Merchants and travelers carrying ready cash may not exceed ten strings.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants and travelers could carry no more than ten strings of ready cash.

sentences.zh: 所司籍辨鈔人以防偽冒。

translations.literal: The responsible offices register note authenticators to guard against counterfeiting and fraud.
