translations.idiomatic: Authorities registered note authenticators to prevent forgery and fraud.

sentences.zh: 品官及民家存留見錢，比舊減其數，若舊有見錢多者，許送官易鈔，十貫以上不得出京。

translations.literal: Ranked officials and common households retaining ready cash, compared with the old [limits] have their amounts reduced; if previously holding much ready cash, permitted to deliver to government and exchange for notes; ten strings and above may not leave the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Cash holdings for officials and households were cut below previous limits. Those with large reserves could exchange surplus cash for notes at the treasury, but amounts of ten strings or more could not be taken out of the capital.

sentences.zh: 」又定制，按察司以鈔法流通為稱職，而河北按察使斜不出巡按所給券應得鈔一貫，以難支用，命取見錢。

translations.literal: " Again regulations were set: surveillance commissions were graded competent by note circulation; but Hebei Surveillance Commissioner Xie Bu-Chu on his inspection route, for vouchers entitling one string in notes, because difficult to use, was ordered to take ready cash.
translations.idiomatic: New rules tied surveillance commissioners' performance ratings to note circulation. But Hebei commissioner Xie Bu-Chu, finding a one-string note from his travel voucher impractical on inspection rounds, demanded cash instead.

sentences.zh: 御史以沮壞鈔法劾之，上曰：「糾察之官乃先壞法，情不可恕。

translations.literal: Censors impeached him for obstructing and ruining the note system; the emperor said: "The very officials charged with oversight have first broken the law—the circumstances cannot be forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: Censors impeached him for undermining the note system. The emperor said, "An inspector who breaks the law first cannot be forgiven.

sentences.zh: 」杖之七十，削官一階，解職。

translations.literal: " He was beaten seventy blows, one rank stripped, dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He received seventy blows, lost one rank, and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書高汝礪言：「鈔法務在必行，府州縣鎮宜各籍辨鈔人，給以條印，聽與人辨驗，隨貫量給二錢，貫例雖多，六錢即止。

translations.literal: Revenue Minister Gao Ruli said: "The note system must be enforced without fail; prefectures, districts, counties, and market towns should each register note authenticators, give them official seals, permit them to authenticate for others, by string measure give two cash per string; though the string denomination be many, six cash is the limit."
translations.idiomatic: Revenue Minister Gao Ruli urged strict enforcement: every prefecture, district, county, and town should register note authenticators, issue them official seals, and allow them to verify notes for the public at two cash per string, capped at six cash regardless of denomination.

sentences.zh: 每朝官出使，則令體究通滯以聞。

translations.literal: Whenever a court official goes on mission, order them to investigate circulation and stagnation and report.
translations.idiomatic: Every court envoy was to investigate local note circulation and report back.

sentences.zh: 民間舊有宋會子，亦令同見錢用，十貫以上不許持行。

translations.literal: Among the people old Song hui notes exist; also order them used equally with ready cash; ten strings and above not permitted to be carried for travel.
translations.idiomatic: Old Song hui notes were allowed alongside cash, but holdings of ten strings or more could not be carried on the road.

sentences.zh: 榷鹽許用銀絹，余市易及俸，並用交鈔，其奇數以小鈔足之，應支銀絹而不足者亦以鈔給之。

translations.literal: Salt monopoly permits use of silver and silk; remaining trade and salaries all use exchange notes; odd amounts made up with small notes; where silver and silk should be disbursed but insufficient, also give in notes.
translations.idiomatic: Salt monopoly payments could still be in silver or silk; all other trade and salaries had to use exchange notes, with small notes covering odd amounts and notes substituted where silver or silk ran short.

sentences.zh: 」上遣近侍諭旨尚書省：「今既以按察司鈔法通快為稱職，否則為不稱職，仍于州府司縣官給由內，明書所犯之數，但犯鈔法者雖監察御史舉其能幹，亦不准用。

translations.literal: " The emperor sent a close attendant to instruct the Secretariat: "Now that surveillance commissions' smooth note circulation counts as competent, otherwise incompetent, moreover in the credentials given to prefecture, district, and county officials, clearly write the number of violations; but those who violate the note law—even if surveillance censors recommend their capability—are not permitted to be appointed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor instructed the Secretariat that surveillance commissioners would be judged competent only if notes circulated smoothly. Violations had to be recorded on officials' service credentials, and anyone who had broken the note law could not be appointed even with a censor's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 」十月，楊序言：「交鈔料號不明，年月故暗，雖令赴庫易新，然外路無設定庫司，欲易無所，遠者直須赴都。

translations.literal: " Tenth month, Yang Xu memorialized: "Exchange notes' serial numbers unclear, years and months worn and faded; although ordered to go to treasuries for new exchange, yet on outer routes no established treasury offices—wanting exchange, nowhere to go; the distant must go straight to the capital."
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Yang Xu reported that worn notes had illegible serial numbers and dates. Though holders could redeem them at treasuries, remote regions had no designated offices, forcing distant subjects to travel all the way to the capital.

sentences.zh: 」上以問汝礪，對曰：「隨處州府庫內，各有辨鈔庫子，鈔雖弊不偽，亦可收納。

translations.literal: " The emperor questioned Ruli; he replied: "Everywhere in prefecture and district treasuries, each has note-authenticating treasury clerks; notes though worn, if not counterfeit, can also be received."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Gao Ruli, who replied that every prefectural treasury had authenticating clerks who would accept worn but genuine notes.

sentences.zh: 去都遠之城邑，既有設置合同換錢，客旅經之皆可相易。

translations.literal: In towns far from the capital, where contract currency exchange is already established, travelers passing through can all exchange with each other.
translations.idiomatic: In towns far from the capital, licensed exchange houses already let travelers swap notes along the route.

sentences.zh: 更慮無合同之地，難以易者，令官庫凡納昏鈔者受而不支，於鈔背印記官吏姓名，積半歲赴都易新鈔。

translations.literal: Further fearing places without contracts, difficult to exchange, order official treasuries: all who submit worn notes receive but do not pay out, on the note's back stamp officials' names, accumulate half a year then go to the capital for new notes.
translations.idiomatic: Where no exchange house existed, official treasuries could receive worn notes without immediate payout, stamp officials' names on the backs, and after six months send them to the capital for new notes.

sentences.zh: 如此，則昏鈔有所歸而無滯矣！」

translations.literal: Thus, worn notes would have a destination and no stagnation!"
translations.idiomatic: "That way worn notes have somewhere to go and will not pile up idle!" he said.

sentences.zh: 十一月，上諭戶部官曰：「今鈔法雖行，卿等亦宜審察 ，少有壅滯，即當以聞，勿謂已行而憚改。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, the emperor instructed Revenue officials: "Though the note system is now in force, you too should carefully examine; if the slightest stagnation, immediately report—do not think because it is already in force that you fear to change."
translations.idiomatic: In November the emperor told the Revenue Ministry that even though notes were mandatory, they must report any stagnation at once and not hesitate to propose changes just because the policy was already in place.

sentences.zh: 」汝礪對曰：「今諸處置庫多在公廨內，小民出入頗難，雖有商賈易之，然患鈔本不豐。

translations.literal: " Ruli replied: "Now exchange treasuries everywhere are mostly inside government compounds; common people entering and leaving is quite difficult; though merchants exchange, yet the problem is insufficient note reserves."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ruli replied that treasuries inside government compounds were hard for common people to reach, and even merchant exchange was hampered by thin note reserves.

sentences.zh: 比者河北西路轉運司言，一富民首其當存留錢外，見錢十四萬貫。

translations.literal: Recently Hebei West Route Transport Office reported: one wealthy household reported that beyond what should be retained, ready cash of one hundred forty thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the Hebei West transport office reported one wealthy man who admitted to holding 140,000 strings of cash beyond the retention limit.

sentences.zh: 它路臆或有如此者，臣等謂宜令州縣委官及庫典，於市肆要處置庫支換。

translations.literal: Other routes presumably may have such cases; we your ministers say it is appropriate to order districts and counties to delegate officials and treasury managers, at key market locations establish treasuries for exchange.
translations.idiomatic: Other regions surely had similar hoards. He proposed that counties post officials and treasurers at busy market sites to run exchange offices.

sentences.zh: 以出首之錢為鈔本，十萬戶以上州府，給三萬貫，以次為差，易鈔者人不得過二貫。

translations.literal: Using self-reported money as note reserves; for prefectures of one hundred thousand households and above, supply thirty thousand strings, in descending gradations; those exchanging notes per person may not exceed two strings.
translations.idiomatic: Confiscated or surrendered cash would fund note reserves—30,000 strings for prefectures over 100,000 households, scaled down for smaller ones—and no one could exchange more than two strings at a time.

sentences.zh: 以所得工墨錢充庫典食直，仍令州府佐貳及轉運司官一員提控。

translations.literal: Use collected processing-and-ink fees to cover treasury managers' sustenance pay; still order one assistant prefect and one transport office official to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: Processing fees would pay the treasurers' wages, with a deputy prefect and a transport official supervising each office.

sentences.zh: 」上是之，遂命移庫於市肆之會，令民以鈔易錢。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved, then ordered treasuries moved to market intersections, permitting the people to exchange notes for cash.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and ordered treasuries moved to market crossroads so people could exchange notes for cash.

sentences.zh: 是月，敕捕獲偽造交鈔者，皆以交鈔為賞。

translations.literal: That month, an edict: those capturing counterfeiters of exchange notes—all rewarded in exchange notes.
translations.idiomatic: That month rewards for capturing counterfeiters were paid in exchange notes.

sentences.zh: 時復議更鈔法，上從高汝礪言，命在官大鈔更不許出。

translations.literal: At the time re-debating changing the note system, the emperor followed Gao Ruli's words, ordering large notes in government [hands] no longer permitted to be disbursed.
translations.idiomatic: Debating further reforms, the emperor adopted Gao Ruli's plan to stop paying out large-denomination notes from government treasuries.

sentences.zh: 聽民以五貫十貫例者赴庫易小鈔，欲得錢者五貫內與一緡，十貫內與兩緡，惟遼東從便。

translations.literal: Permit the people holding five-string and ten-string denomination notes to go to treasuries and exchange for small notes; those wanting cash—in five-string notes give one string within, in ten-string notes give two strings within; only Liaodong at convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Holders of five- and ten-string notes could redeem them for small notes at treasuries, or take partial cash—one string from a five-string note, two from a ten-string note—except in Liaodong, where rules were relaxed.

sentences.zh: 河南、陝西、山東及它行鈔諸路，院務諸稅及諸科名錢，並以三分為率，一分納十貫例者，二分五貫例者，餘並收見錢。

translations.literal: Henan, Shaanxi, Shandong and other routes issuing notes—all wine-shop taxes and assorted named fees, all at one-third rate: one part pay ten-string denomination, two parts five-string denomination; the remainder all collect ready cash.
translations.idiomatic: In Henan, Shaanxi, Shandong, and other note-issuing circuits, a third of wine-shop and commercial taxes had to be paid in notes—one part in ten-string notes and two parts in five-string notes—with the rest in cash.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，以京師鈔滯，定所司賞罰格。

translations.literal: Eighth year first month, because capital notes stagnated, set reward-and-punishment standards for responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: Taihe 8, first month: stagnation in the capital prompted standardized rewards and penalties for responsible offices.

sentences.zh: 時新制，按察司及州縣官，例以鈔通滯為升降。

translations.literal: At the time new regulations: surveillance commissions and district and county officials, by rule use note circulation and stagnation for promotion and demotion.
translations.idiomatic: New rules tied promotions for surveillance commissioners and local officials to how well notes circulated.

sentences.zh: 遂命監察御史賞罰同外道按察司，大興府警巡院官同外路州縣官。

translations.literal: Thereupon ordered surveillance censors' rewards and punishments same as outer-route surveillance commissions; Daxing Prefecture patrol-yard officials same as outer-route district and county officials.
translations.idiomatic: Capital surveillance censors and Daxing patrol officials were subjected to the same note-circulation incentives as their provincial counterparts.

sentences.zh: 是月，收毀大鈔，行小鈔。

translations.literal: That month, collect and destroy large notes, circulate small notes.
translations.idiomatic: That month large notes were withdrawn and small notes put into circulation.

sentences.zh: 八月，從遼東按察司楊雲翼言，以咸平、東京兩路商旅所集，遂從都南例，一貫以上皆用交鈔，不得用錢。

translations.literal: Eighth month, following Liaodong Surveillance Commissioner Yang Yunyi's memorial, because Xianping and Tokyo two routes are where merchants and travelers gather, then follow the capital-south precedent: one string and above all use exchange notes, may not use cash.
translations.idiomatic: In August, on Yang Yunyi's advice, Xianping and Tokyo routes—major merchant hubs—followed southern capital rules requiring notes for any transaction of one string or more.

sentences.zh: 十月，孫鐸又言：「民間鈔多，正宜收斂，院務稅諸名錢，可盡收鈔，秋夏稅納本色外，亦令收鈔，不拘貫例。

translations.literal: Tenth month, Sun Duo again memorialized: "Among the people notes are many—it is exactly the time to absorb them; wine-shop taxes and assorted named fees can all collect notes; autumn and summer taxes beyond payment in kind, also order note collection, not bound by denomination."
translations.idiomatic: In October Sun Duo argued that with notes abundant, the state should absorb them—accepting notes for all commercial taxes and for summer and autumn levies beyond grain payments, regardless of denomination.

sentences.zh: 農民知之則漸重鈔，可以流通。

translations.literal: When farmers know this, gradually they will value notes, and circulation is possible.
translations.idiomatic: Once farmers understood this, they would begin to value notes and circulation would improve.

sentences.zh: 比來州縣抑配市肆買鈔，徒增騷擾，可罷諸處創設鈔局，止令赴省庫換易。

translations.literal: Recently districts and counties coerced market shops to buy notes, merely increasing harassment; can abolish note bureaus newly established everywhere, only order [people] to go to provincial treasuries to exchange.
translations.idiomatic: County coercion forcing shops to buy notes had only caused trouble; he urged abolishing local note bureaus and limiting exchange to provincial treasuries.

sentences.zh: 今小鈔各限路分，亦甚未便，可令通用。

translations.literal: Now small notes each limited by route—also very inconvenient; can order universal circulation.
translations.idiomatic: Route-specific small notes were inconvenient; he proposed making them valid everywhere.

sentences.zh: 」上命亟行之。

translations.literal: " The emperor ordered prompt implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered these measures implemented at once.

sentences.zh: 十二月，宰臣奏：「舊制，內外官兵俸皆給鈔，其必用錢以足數者，可以十分為率，軍兵給三分，官員承應人給二分，多不過十貫。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, chief ministers memorialized: "Old regulations: internal and external military and civil salaries all paid in notes; where cash must be used to complete the amount, may take ten parts as rate—soldiers given three parts, officials and attendants given two parts, mostly not exceeding ten strings."
translations.idiomatic: In December ministers reported that salaries were paid in notes, with up to 30% in cash for soldiers and 20% for officials and attendants, capped at ten strings.

sentences.zh: 凡前所收大鈔，俟至通行當複計造，其終須當精緻以圖經久。

translations.literal: All large notes previously collected—wait until they circulate again, then plan re-minting; ultimately must be refined and fine to seek long endurance.
translations.idiomatic: Collected large notes would be reissued once circulation recovered, and future printings had to be refined for durability.

sentences.zh: 民間舊鈔故暗者，乞許于所在庫易新。

translations.literal: Old notes among the people worn and faded—request permission to exchange for new at local treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: They asked that worn notes be redeemable for new ones at local treasuries.

sentences.zh: 若官吏勢要之家有賤買交鈔，而於院務換錢興販者，以違制論。

translations.literal: If officials or powerful families buy exchange notes cheaply, then at wine shops exchange for cash to engage in resale—forfeit as violation of imperial orders.
translations.idiomatic: Officials or powerful families who bought notes cheaply and resold them for cash at wine shops would be charged with violating imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 複遣官分路巡察，其限錢過數雖許奴婢以告，乃有所屬默令其主藏匿不以實首者，可令按察司察之。

translations.literal: Again send officials on divided routes to inspect; though excess cash beyond limits permits slaves and servants to report, yet if dependents silently order their masters to conceal and not report truthfully—can order surveillance commissions to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Inspectors would tour the routes again. Though servants could report hidden cash hoards, surveillance commissions were empowered to investigate masters who silenced them.

sentences.zh: 若舊限已滿，當更展五十日，許再令變易鈔引諸物。

translations.literal: If the old deadline has passed, should extend fifty more days, permit again exchanging notes and obtaining various goods.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed extending the conversion deadline by fifty days so people could again exchange notes and goods.

sentences.zh: 」是制既行之後，章宗尋崩，衛紹王繼立，大安三年會河之役，至以八十四車為軍賞，兵衄國殘，不遑救弊，交鈔之輕幾于不能市易矣。

translations.literal: " After this system was implemented, Emperor Zhangzong soon died, Emperor Weishao succeeded; third year of Da'an, Battle of Hui River—reaching the point of eighty-four cartloads as military rewards; army defeated, state crippled, no time to remedy abuses; exchange notes' lightness nearly made market trade impossible.
translations.idiomatic: After these reforms Zhangzong died and Weishao succeeded. At the Da'an 3 Battle of Hui River the state paid military bonuses in eighty-four cartloads of notes; defeat left the dynasty too battered to fix monetary abuses, and notes sank so far they could barely buy anything.

sentences.zh: 至宣宗貞祐二年二月，思有以重之，乃更作二十貫至百貫例交鈔，又造二百貫至千貫例者。

translations.literal: Reaching Emperor Xuanzong Zhenyou second year second month, thinking to add weight, then newly made twenty-string to hundred-string denomination exchange notes, also minted two-hundred-string to thousand-string denomination ones.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyou 2 (1214), second month, Xuanzong tried to restore value by issuing new notes from twenty to one hundred strings, and even two hundred to one thousand strings.

sentences.zh: 然自泰和以來，凡更交鈔，初雖重，不數年則輕而不行，至是則愈更而愈滯矣。

translations.literal: Yet from the Taihe reign onward, every time exchange notes were changed, initially though heavy, within a few years they became light and would not circulate—to this point the more changes the more stagnation.
translations.idiomatic: Since Taihe every note reform had briefly strengthened currency only to see it depreciate within years; now each new issue made circulation worse.

sentences.zh: 南遷之後，國蹙民困，軍旅不息，供億無度，輕又甚焉。

translations.literal: After southward relocation, the state cramped, the people afflicted; armies unceasing; supplies without measure—lightness again even more severe.
translations.idiomatic: After the court moved south, a shrinking state, exhausted people, endless warfare, and limitless spending drove notes to new depths of debasement.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，河東宣撫使胥鼎上言曰：「今之物重，其弊在於鈔窒，有出而無入也。

translations.literal: Third year fourth month, Hedong Military Commissioner Xu Ding memorialized: "Today's goods heavy—the abuse lies in notes' stagnation, disbursement without intake."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year three, Hedong commissioner Xu Ding wrote, "Prices are high because notes stagnate: the state pays them out but does not take them back in."

sentences.zh: 雖院務稅增收數倍，而所納皆十貫例大鈔，此何益哉？

translations.literal: Though wine-shop taxes increase collection several fold, yet what is paid in are all ten-string denomination large notes—what benefit is this?
translations.idiomatic: Commercial taxes had been raised several times, but payment came in worthless ten-string notes—what good did that do?

sentences.zh: 今十貫例者民間甚多，以無所歸，故市易多用見錢，而鈔每貫僅直一錢，曾不及工墨之費。

translations.literal: Now ten-string denomination ones are many among the people; because they have nowhere to go, market trade mostly uses ready cash; yet notes each string worth barely one cash coin, not even reaching processing-and-ink costs.
translations.idiomatic: Ten-string notes piled up in private hands with nowhere to go, so markets ran on cash while each string of notes traded for a single coin—less than the printing fee.

sentences.zh: 臣愚謂，宜權禁見錢，且令計司以軍須為名，量民力征斂，則泉貨流通，而物價平矣。

translations.literal: Your minister foolishly thinks: temporarily ban ready cash, and order the accounting offices under the name of military requirements to levy according to people's strength—then currency will circulate and goods prices level.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed temporarily banning cash and levying supplies in the name of military needs according to ability—thus restoring circulation and stabilizing prices.

sentences.zh: 」自是，錢貨不用，富家內困藏鏹之限，外弊交鈔屢變，皆至窘敗，謂之「坐化」。

translations.literal: " From this, cash currency unused; wealthy families inwardly distressed by cash-hoarding limits, outwardly afflicted by exchange notes' repeated changes—all reached destitution, called "sitting transformation."
translations.idiomatic: Cash fell out of use. Wealthy families chafed at hoarding limits while repeated note changes eroded their fortunes—a ruin known as "sitting transformation," watching wealth evaporate in place.

sentences.zh: 商人往往舟運貿易于江淮，錢多入于宋矣。

translations.literal: Merchants often shipped by boat to trade in the Yangtze and Huai; much cash entered Song territory.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants shipped goods to the Yangtze-Huai region, draining coin into Song territory.

sentences.zh: 宋人以為喜，而金人不禁也，識者惜其既不能重無用之楮，而又棄自古流行之寶焉。

translations.literal: Song people took it as joy, yet Jin people did not prohibit it; the knowledgeable grieved that they could neither restore worthless paper nor yet abandoned the treasure circulating since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: The Song welcomed the influx while the Jin did nothing. Observers lamented that the dynasty could neither restore worthless paper nor keep the coin that had circulated for millennia.

sentences.zh: 五月，權西安軍節度使烏林達與言：「關陝軍多，供億不足，所仰交鈔則取于京師，徒成煩費，乞降板就造便。

translations.literal: Fifth month, Acting Xi'an Military Commissioner Wulinda Yu said: "Guanshaan has many troops, supplies insufficient; the exchange notes relied upon are taken from the capital—merely creating trouble and expense; request lowering the printing blocks for local manufacture at convenience."
translations.idiomatic: In May acting Xi'an commissioner Wulinda Yu argued that Guan-Shaan's large garrison could not afford to haul notes from the capital and asked permission to print locally.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「懷州舊鐵錢钜萬，今既無用，願貫為甲，以給戰士。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Huai Prefecture's old iron cash amounting to tens of thousands—now useless—we wish to string them into armor to supply warriors."
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed stringing Huai Prefecture's hoard of obsolete iron cash into armor for soldiers.

sentences.zh: 」時有司輕罪議罰，率以鐵贖，而當罪不平，遂命贖銅計贓皆以銀價為准。

translations.literal: " At the time responsible offices for minor offenses deliberated penalties, mostly using iron for redemption—but the crime did not match evenly; thereupon ordered copper redemption and compensation calculations all take silver price as standard.
translations.idiomatic: Minor penalties had been commuted in iron at uneven rates, so the court standardized copper fines and compensation by silver value.

sentences.zh: 六月，敕議交鈔利便。

translations.literal: Sixth month, edict to deliberate advantages and convenience of exchange notes.
translations.idiomatic: In June the court ordered a review of note policy.

sentences.zh: 七月，改交鈔名為「貞祐寶券」，仍立沮阻罪。

translations.literal: Seventh month, changed exchange notes' name to "Zhenyou Precious Certificates," also established obstruction offenses.
translations.idiomatic: In July notes were renamed "Zhenyou Precious Certificates" and penalties were set for obstructing their use.

sentences.zh: 九月，御史台言：「自多故以來，全藉交鈔以助軍需，然所入不及所出，則其價浸減，卒無法以禁，此必然之理也。

translations.literal: Ninth month, the Censorate said: "Since many troubles began, wholly relying on exchange notes to aid military needs; yet intake does not match outflow—then their value gradually diminishes, ultimately no method to prohibit it; this is inevitable principle."
translations.idiomatic: In September the Censorate observed that since the crises began the state had relied on notes for military supply, but when outflow exceeded intake their value inevitably fell with no way to stop it.

sentences.zh: 近用'貞祐寶券'以革其弊，又慮既多而民輕，與舊鈔無異也，乃令民間市易悉從時估，嚴立罪賞，期於必行，遂使商旅不行，四方之物不敢入。

translations.literal: Recently using 'Zhenyou Precious Certificates' to reform their abuses, again fearing that once numerous the people would treat them lightly—no different from old notes—thereupon ordered among the people market trade all follow current appraisals, strictly establish crime and reward, expecting mandatory enforcement—thus causing merchants and travelers not to travel, goods from the four directions not daring to enter.
translations.idiomatic: The new Zhenyou Precious Certificates were meant to fix the problem, but fearing overissue would debase them like the old notes, the court forced all trade to follow official price appraisals with harsh penalties—merchants stopped traveling and goods ceased to flow in.

sentences.zh: 夫京師百萬之眾，日費不貲，物價寧不日貴耶？

translations.literal: The capital's population of a million—daily expense incalculable—will goods prices not daily grow dear?
translations.idiomatic: With a million mouths to feed in the capital, how could prices not rise by the day?

sentences.zh: 且時估月再定之，而民間價旦暮不一，今有司強之，而市肆盡閉。

translations.literal: Moreover current appraisals are reset twice monthly, yet among the people prices differ morning and evening; now responsible offices force them, and market shops all close.
translations.idiomatic: Official prices were reset twice a month while market prices shifted daily; forced compliance had shut the shops entirely.

sentences.zh: 復議搜括隱匿，必令如估鬻之，則京師之物指日盡，而百姓重困矣。

translations.literal: Again deliberating search and seizure of concealed goods, mandating sale at appraised prices—then the capital's goods within days exhausted, and the common people doubly afflicted.
translations.idiomatic: Plans to seize hidden stock and sell it at official prices would empty the capital within days and crush the people further.

sentences.zh: 臣等謂，惟官和買計贓之類可用時估，餘宜從便。

translations.literal: We your ministers say: only official purchases and compensation calculations and the like may use current appraisals; the rest should follow convenience.
translations.idiomatic: They argued that official price controls should apply only to government purchases and compensation cases, leaving ordinary trade free.

sentences.zh: 」制可。

translations.literal: " The regulation was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 十二月，上聞近京郡縣多糴于京師，穀價翔踴，令尚書省集戶部、講議所、開封府、轉運司，議所以制之者。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, the emperor heard that near-capital districts and counties mostly purchased grain in the capital; grain prices soaring—ordered the Secretariat to assemble Revenue, the Deliberation Office, Kaifeng Prefecture, and the Transport Office to deliberate means of controlling it.
translations.idiomatic: In December the emperor learned that nearby counties were buying grain in the capital, driving prices skyward, and ordered the Secretariat, Revenue Ministry, deliberation office, Kaifeng prefecture, and transport commission to find a remedy.

sentences.zh: 戶部及講議所言，以五鬥出城者可闌糴其半，轉運司謂宜悉禁其出，上從開封府議，謂：「寶券初行時，民甚重之。

translations.literal: Revenue and the Deliberation Office said: those taking five dou out of the city may be blocked from buying half their grain; the Transport Office said all outbound grain should be forbidden; the emperor followed Kaifeng Prefecture's proposal, saying: "When precious certificates first circulated, the people valued them highly."
translations.idiomatic: Revenue and the deliberation office proposed blocking half the grain purchases of anyone exporting five dou from the city; the transport office wanted a total ban. The emperor sided with Kaifeng prefecture, noting that when precious certificates first appeared the people had valued them highly.

sentences.zh: 但以河北、陝西諸路所支既多，人遂輕之。

translations.literal: But because Hebei, Shaanxi, and other routes had disbursed so many, people then treated them lightly.
translations.idiomatic: But heavy disbursements in Hebei, Shaanxi, and other circuits had since made people treat them lightly.

sentences.zh: 商賈爭收入京，以市金銀，銀價昂，穀亦隨之。

translations.literal: Merchants and traders competed to bring [certificates] into the capital to buy gold and silver; silver prices rose high, grain followed likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants rushed notes into the capital to buy gold and silver, driving up silver prices and grain along with them.

sentences.zh: 若令寶券路各殊制，則不可複入河南，則河南金銀賤而穀自輕。

translations.literal: If precious certificates each route have separate systems, then they cannot again enter Henan—then Henan's gold and silver would be cheap and grain naturally light.
translations.idiomatic: If each circuit issued certificates under separate rules, they could not circulate back into Henan—where silver would cheapen and grain prices would fall.

sentences.zh: 若直閉京城粟不出，則外亦自守，不復入京，穀當益貴。

translations.literal: If the capital's grain is directly sealed and not permitted out, then the outer regions also hold their own and do not again enter the capital—grain should grow even dearer.
translations.idiomatic: Sealing the capital's grain supply would make the provinces hoard their own and stop shipping to the capital, making grain even costlier.

sentences.zh: 宜諭郡縣小民，毋妄增價，官為定制，務從其便。」

translations.literal: It is appropriate to instruct districts and counties' common people not to raise prices recklessly; the government should set regulations, striving to follow convenience."
translations.idiomatic: County folk should be warned against price gouging while the government set fair rules for everyone's convenience."

sentences.zh: 四年正月，監察御史田迥秀言：「國家調度皆資寶券，行才數月，又複壅滯，非約束不嚴、奉行不謹也。

translations.literal: Fourth year first month, Surveillance Censor Tian Jiongxiu said: "The state's fiscal allocations all rely on precious certificates; in circulation only a few months, again stagnation—not because regulations are lax or enforcement careless."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year four, censor Tian Jiongxiu argued that although state finances depended on precious certificates, they had stagnated again within months—not from lax enforcement.

sentences.zh: 夫錢幣欲流通，必輕重相權、散斂有術而後可。

translations.literal: For currency to desire circulation, light and heavy must mutually balance, release and absorption have method—only then is it possible.
translations.idiomatic: Currency circulates only when issuance and recall are balanced with deliberate technique.

sentences.zh: 今之患在出太多、入太少爾。

translations.literal: Today's affliction lies in disbursement too much, intake too little—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: The problem was too much paid out and too little taken back in.

sentences.zh: 若隨時裁損所支，而增其所收，庶乎或可也。

translations.literal: If according to the times cut disbursements and increase collections, perhaps it may be possible.
translations.idiomatic: Cut spending and increase collections as conditions required, and the system might recover.

sentences.zh: 」因條五事，一曰省冗官吏，二曰損酒使司，三曰節兵俸，四曰罷寄治官，五曰酒稅及納粟補官皆當用寶券。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he listed five items: first, reduce redundant officials; second, cut wine commissioner offices; third, economize military salaries; fourth, abolish supernumerary posted officials; fifth, wine taxes and grain payments for purchased office should all use precious certificates.
translations.idiomatic: He offered five reforms: trim redundant officials, cut wine-tax offices, reduce military pay, abolish supernumerary posts, and require precious certificates for wine taxes and grain payments for purchased office.

sentences.zh: 詔酒稅從大定之舊，餘皆不從。

translations.literal: An edict: wine taxes follow the Dading-era old practice; the rest all not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The court kept wine taxes on the old Dading basis and rejected the rest.

sentences.zh: 尋又更定捕獲偽造寶券官賞。

translations.literal: Soon after again revised official rewards for capturing counterfeiters of precious certificates.
translations.idiomatic: Official rewards for catching counterfeiters of precious certificates were soon revised.

sentences.zh: 三月，翰林侍講學士趙秉文言：「比者寶券滯塞，蓋朝廷將議更張，已而妄傳不用，因之抑遏，漸至廢絕，此乃權歸小民也。

translations.literal: Third month, Hanlin Attendant Lecturer Zhao Bingwen said: "Recently precious certificates stagnated—presumably because the court was about to deliberate reform; then false rumors spread that they would not be used; thereby suppressed, gradually reaching abandonment—this is authority returning to the common people."
translations.idiomatic: In March Hanlin lecturer Zhao Bingwen said recent stagnation stemmed from rumors of impending reform; panic hoarding had nearly killed the notes, handing market power to private traders.

sentences.zh: 自遷汴以來，廢回易務，臣愚謂當複置，令職官通市道者掌之，給銀鈔粟麥縑帛之類，權其低昂而出納之。

translations.literal: Since relocating to Bian, the Exchange Office was abolished; your minister foolishly thinks it should be restored, ordering officials versed in market ways to manage it, supplying silver, notes, grain, wheat, silk, and cloth and the like, weighing their rise and fall and disbursing and receiving them.
translations.idiomatic: Since the move to Bian the state exchange office had been abolished; he urged restoring it under market-savvy officials who would trade silver, notes, grain, and cloth at adjusted prices.

sentences.zh: 仍自選良監當官營為之，若半年無過，及券法通流，則聽所指任便差遣。

translations.literal: Still personally select capable supervising officials to operate it; if within half a year no fault, and the certificate system circulates smoothly, then permit appointment wherever they designate at convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Capable supervisors should run it; after six months without fault, with notes circulating smoothly, they could be appointed wherever they chose.

sentences.zh: 」詔議行之。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the proposal studied and carried out.

sentences.zh: 四月，河東行省胥鼎言：「交鈔貴乎流通，今諸路所造不充所出，不以術收之，不無缺誤。

translations.literal: Fourth month, Hedong Branch Secretariat Xu Ding said: "Exchange notes are valued in circulation; now what the various routes mint does not meet disbursement; without method to collect them back, there cannot but be shortfalls and errors."
translations.idiomatic: In April Hedong branch secretary Xu Ding warned that notes mattered only in circulation, yet provincial minting could not keep pace with payouts and nothing was being done to recall them.

sentences.zh: 宜量民力征斂，以裨軍用。

translations.literal: It is appropriate to levy according to the people's strength to supplement military use.
translations.idiomatic: He urged levies scaled to local capacity to support the army.

sentences.zh: 河中宣撫司亦以寶券多出，民不之貴，乞驗民貧富征之。

translations.literal: The Hezhong Military Commission also, because precious certificates are issued in excess and the people do not value them, requests assessing the people's wealth and poverty to levy accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The Hezhong military commission likewise cited overissue and public distrust, asking for levies graded by wealth.

sentences.zh: 雖為陝西，若一體徵收，則彼中所有日湊於河東，與不斂何異？

translations.literal: Although it is Shaanxi, if levied uniformly, then what is there would daily drain toward Hedong—how is that different from not collecting?
translations.idiomatic: Even in Shaanxi, a uniform levy would simply funnel its resources into Hedong—no different from collecting nothing at all.

sentences.zh: 又河北寶券以不許行于河南，由是愈滯。

translations.literal: Moreover Hebei precious certificates, because not permitted to circulate in Henan, thereby stagnate all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei certificates also stagnated because they were barred from Henan.

sentences.zh: 」宰臣謂：「昨以河北寶券，商旅齎販繼踵南渡，遂致物價翔踴，乃權宜限以路分。

translations.literal: " The chief ministers said: "Previously because of Hebei precious certificates, merchants and travelers carrying goods for trade followed one after another south across the river, thus causing goods prices to soar—therefore as expedient measure limited by route division."
translations.idiomatic: Ministers replied that Hebei certificates had once flooded south with merchants, spiking prices, so route limits had been a temporary fix.

sentences.zh: 今鼎既以本路用度繁殷，欲征軍須錢，宜從所請。

translations.literal: Now Ding, because this route's expenditures are heavy and numerous, wishes to levy military-supply money—should follow his request.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xu Ding's route faced heavy expenses and sought military levies, his request should be granted.

sentences.zh: 若陝西可征與否，詔令行省議定而後行。

translations.literal: As for whether Shaanxi may be levied, an edict orders the branch secretariat to deliberate and decide before implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Whether Shaanxi should be levied was left for the branch secretariat to decide.

sentences.zh: 」五月，上以河北州府官錢散失，多在民間，命尚書省經畫之。

translations.literal: " Fifth month, the emperor, because Hebei prefectures' and districts' official cash was scattered and lost, mostly among the people, ordered the Secretariat to plan and manage it.
translations.idiomatic: In May the emperor learned that much official cash in Hebei had leaked into private hands and ordered the Secretariat to recover it.

sentences.zh: 八月，平章高琪奏：「軍興以來，用度不貲，惟賴寶券，然所入不敷所出，是以浸輕，今千錢之券僅直數錢，隨造隨盡，工物日增，不有以救之，弊將滋甚。

translations.literal: Eighth month, Grand Councilor Gao Qi memorialized: "Since military campaigns began, expenditures incalculable, relying solely on precious certificates; yet intake does not cover outflow, therefore gradually lightening—now a thousand-cash certificate worth barely several cash, minted and exhausted as soon as made, labor and materials daily increasing—without remedy, abuses will grow severe."
translations.idiomatic: In August Grand Councilor Gao Qi reported that since the wars began the state had lived on precious certificates, but outflow exceeded intake until a thousand-cash note traded for pennies; printing costs rose daily and the abuse would worsen without reform.

sentences.zh: 宜更造新券，與舊券權為子母而兼行之，庶工物俱省，而用不乏。

translations.literal: It is appropriate to newly mint fresh certificates, with old certificates temporarily as parent and child circulating together—perhaps labor and materials both saved, and use not lacking.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed new notes to circulate alongside old ones as parent and child denominations, saving printing costs while keeping supply adequate.

sentences.zh: 」濮王守純以下皆憚改，奏曰：「自古軍旅之費皆取于民，向朝廷以小鈔殊輕，權更寶券，而複禁用錢。

translations.literal: " Prince of Pu Shou Chun and those below all feared change, memorializing: "Since antiquity military expenses all come from the people; previously the court, because small notes were especially light, temporarily changed to precious certificates, and again forbade cash use."
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Pu Shou Chun and others resisted further change, noting that armies had always been funded by the people; when small notes collapsed the court had swapped in precious certificates and banned cash.

sentences.zh: 小民淺慮，謂楮幣易壞，不若錢可久，於是得錢則珍藏，而券則亟用之，惟恐破裂而至於廢也。

translations.literal: Common people with shallow thinking say paper currency easily spoils, not like cash that lasts; thus when they obtain cash they hoard it, while certificates they use urgently, only fearing tearing and reaching abandonment.
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary people, thinking paper fragile and coin durable, hoarded cash and spent certificates as fast as possible for fear they would tear and become worthless.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷知支而不知收，所以錢日貴而券日輕。

translations.literal: Now the court knows disbursement but not collection—therefore cash daily dearer and certificates daily lighter.
translations.idiomatic: The court kept paying out without taking notes back in, so cash grew dearer and certificates cheaper by the day.

sentences.zh: 然則券之輕非民輕之，國家致之然也。

translations.literal: Thus then, the lightness of certificates is not the people making them light—the state has brought it to be so.
translations.idiomatic: The notes were not undervalued because the people despised them—the state itself had made them worthless.

sentences.zh: 不若量其所支複斂於民，出入迴圈，則彼知為必用之物，而知愛重矣。

translations.literal: Better to measure what is disbursed and again collect from the people, outflow and inflow circling—then they will know it as a thing necessarily used, and know to cherish and value it.
translations.idiomatic: Better to calibrate disbursements and levy notes back from the people in a circular flow, so they would see them as essential currency and treat them with respect.

sentences.zh: 今徒患輕而即欲更造，不惟信令不行，且恐新券之輕複同舊券也。

translations.literal: Now merely fretting over lightness and immediately wishing to remint—not only will trust and commands not be enforced, but I fear the new certificates' lightness will again match the old certificates.
translations.idiomatic: To panic over devaluation and rush to remint would undermine public trust and likely leave the new notes as worthless as the old.

sentences.zh: 」既而，隴州防禦使完顏宇及陝西行省令史惠吉繼言券法之弊。

translations.literal: " Shortly after, Long Prefecture defense commissioner Wanyan Yu and Shaanxi Branch Secretariat clerk Hui Ji successively spoke of the abuses of the certificate law.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Long Prefecture Defense Commissioner Wanyan Yu and Shaanxi Branch Secretariat clerk Hui Ji also weighed in on the failings of the note system.

sentences.zh: 宇請姑罷印造，以見在者流通之，若滯塞則驗丁口之多寡、物力之高下而征之。

translations.literal: Yu requested to suspend printing for the time being and circulate what exists; if stagnant and blocked, then examine households' numbers and property's high and low to levy.
translations.idiomatic: Yu urged a halt to new printing and circulation of existing stock, with levies based on household size and wealth if notes piled up unused.

sentences.zh: 吉言：「券者所以救弊一時，非可通流與見錢比，必欲通之，不過多斂少支爾。

translations.literal: Ji said: "Certificates are what remedy abuses for a time—not possible to circulate and compare with ready cash; if one must circulate them, it is nothing but levy much and disburse little."
translations.idiomatic: Ji argued that notes were only a stopgap: they could not circulate like hard coin, and forcing them to would mean collecting far more than was paid out.

sentences.zh: 然斂多則傷民，支少則用不足，二者皆不可。

translations.literal: Yet levy much then harms the people, disburse little then use insufficient—both are impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy collection harmed the populace while meager disbursement left the treasury short—neither course was workable.

sentences.zh: 為今日計，莫若更造，以'貞祐通寶'為名，自百至三千等之為十，聽各路轉運司印造，仍不得過五千貫，與舊券參用，庶乎可也。

translations.literal: For today's reckoning, none better than reminting, with 'Zhenyou Tongbao' as the name, from one hundred to three thousand ranked in ten denominations, hearing each circuit transport commission print, still not exceeding five thousand strings, jointly used with old certificates—perhaps it may do.
translations.idiomatic: For the present crisis he proposed reminting notes called "Zhenyou Tongbao" in ten denominations from one hundred to three thousand cash, printed by circuit transport offices up to five thousand strings each, to circulate alongside the old notes.

sentences.zh: 」詔集百官議。

translations.literal: " An edict convoked all officials to debate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered a full court debate on the matter.

sentences.zh: 戶部侍郎奧屯阿虎、禮部侍郎楊雲翼、郎中蘭芝、刑部侍郎馮鶚皆主更造。

translations.literal: Revenue Vice Minister Outun Ahu, Rites Vice Minister Yang Yunyi, Bureau Director Lanzhi, and Justice Vice Minister Feng E all advocated reminting.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue Vice Minister Outun Ahu, Rites Vice Minister Yang Yunyi, Bureau Director Lanzhi, and Justice Vice Minister Feng E all favored reminting.

sentences.zh: 戶部侍郎高夔、員外郎張師魯、兵部侍郎徒單歐裏白皆請征斂。

translations.literal: Revenue Vice Minister Gao Kui, Vice Director Zhang Shilu, and War Vice Minister Tushan Oulibai all petitioned for collection and levies.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue Vice Minister Gao Kui, Vice Director Zhang Shilu, and War Vice Minister Tushan Oulibai argued for a levy instead.

sentences.zh: 惟戶部尚書蕭貢謂止當如舊，而工部尚書李元輔謂二者可並行。

translations.literal: Only Revenue Minister Xiao Gong said one should simply keep to the old, while Works Minister Li Yuanfu said both could proceed in parallel.
translations.idiomatic: Only Revenue Minister Xiao Gong wanted to keep the existing system; Works Minister Li Yuanfu thought both reminting and levies could proceed together.

sentences.zh: 太子少保張行信亦言不宜更造，但嚴立不行之罪，足矣。

translations.literal: Junior Tutor to the Heir Zhang Xingxin also said reminting was unsuitable—simply strictly establishing the crime of non-circulation would suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Tutor to the Heir Zhang Xingxin also opposed reminting, arguing that stiff penalties for refusing to accept notes would be enough.

sentences.zh: 侍御史趙伯成曰：「更造之法，陰奪民利，其弊甚於征。

translations.literal: Attending Censor Zhao Bocheng said: "The method of reminting covertly seizes the people's profit—its abuse is worse than levying."
translations.idiomatic: Attending Censor Zhao Bocheng said reminting covertly stripped the people of their assets and was worse than a direct levy.

sentences.zh: 征之為法，特徵于農民則不可，若征於市肆商賈之家，是亦敦本抑末之一端。

translations.literal: As for levying as a method—specifically levying from farmers is impossible; if levying from marketplace merchant households, this is also one thread of honoring the root and suppressing the branch.
translations.idiomatic: A levy was tolerable only if it fell on merchants rather than farmers—it would at least serve the policy of favoring agriculture over trade.

sentences.zh: 」刑部主事王壽寧曰：「不然，今之重錢輕券者皆農爾，其斂必先於民而後可。

translations.literal: " Justice Clerk Wang Shouning said: "Not so—now those who value cash and devalue certificates are all farmers; the collection must come first from the people before it can succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Justice Clerk Wang Shouning countered that farmers were the ones hoarding cash and shunning notes, so any collection would inevitably fall on them first.

sentences.zh: 」轉運使王擴曰：「凡論事當究其本，今歲支軍士家口糧四萬余石，如使斯人地著，少寬民力，然後征之，則行之不難。

translations.literal: " Transport Commissioner Wang Kuo said: "Whenever debating affairs one should investigate the root—this year disbursing grain for soldiers' family rations over forty thousand shi; if one makes these people settle locally, slightly loosening the people's strength, then levying—execution would not be difficult."
translations.idiomatic: Transport Commissioner Wang Kuo urged addressing root causes: this year over forty thousand shi of grain had been paid to dependents of garrison troops; if those men were settled locally and the people's burdens eased, a levy would be far easier to enforce.

sentences.zh: 」榷貨司楊貞亦欲節無名之費，罷閑冗之官。

translations.literal: " Monopoly Bureau officer Yang Zhen also wished to cut nameless expenditures and dismiss idle redundant officials.
translations.idiomatic: Monopoly Bureau officer Yang Zhen called for cutting wasteful spending and abolishing redundant posts.

sentences.zh: 或有請鑄大錢以當百，別造小鈔以省費。

translations.literal: Some requested casting large cash to stand for one hundred, separately minting small notes to save expense.
translations.idiomatic: Others proposed casting hundred-cash coins or issuing smaller notes to cut printing costs.

sentences.zh: 或謂縣官當擇人者。

translations.literal: Some said district officials should be chosen for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Still others argued that local magistrates simply needed to be better chosen.

sentences.zh: 獨吏部尚書溫蒂罕思敬上書言：「國家立法，莫不備具，但有司不克奉之而已。

translations.literal: Alone, Personnel Minister Wanyan Sijing memorialized: "The state's laws, none not complete and ready—but the responsible offices cannot uphold them, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Personnel Minister Wanyan Sijing alone submitted a memorial arguing that the laws were adequate but officials simply failed to enforce them.

sentences.zh: 誠使臣得便宜從事，凡外路四品以下官皆許杖決，三品以上奏聞，仍付監察二人弛驛往來，法不必變，民不必征，一號令之，可使上下無不奉法。

translations.literal: Truly if your subject may act expediently as needed, all outer-circuit officials of fourth rank and below permitted corporal punishment decision, third rank and above reported to the throne, still assigning two censors to travel by relay posts back and forth—law need not change, people need not be levied, one command proclaimed, can make high and low none not uphold the law.
translations.idiomatic: If granted discretionary authority to flog fourth-rank officials and below in the provinces, report third-rank offenses to the throne, and deploy two censors on relay courier duty, he could enforce existing law without reminting or levies—one order and all would comply.

sentences.zh: 如其不然，請就重刑。

translations.literal: If it is not so, I request to accept heavy punishment.
translations.idiomatic: If refused, he asked to be punished severely.

sentences.zh: 」上以示宰臣曰：「彼自許如此，試委之可乎？

translations.literal: " The emperor showed this to the chief ministers, saying: "He himself pledges thus—might we try commissioning him?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed this to his chief ministers and asked whether they should give Sijing the assignment he demanded.

sentences.zh: 」宰臣未有以處，而監察御史陳規，完顏素蘭交諍，以為：「事有難行，聖哲猶病之，思敬何為者，徒害人爾。

translations.literal: " The chief ministers had no means to decide, but Censor Chen Gui and Wanyan Sulan argued back and forth, saying: "When affairs are hard to execute, even sages are troubled by them—what is Sijing doing? He merely harms people."
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers could not decide. Censor Chen Gui and Wanyan Sulan objected that even sages struggled with impracticable schemes and accused Sijing of wanting to harm the people.

sentences.zh: 」上以眾議紛紛，月餘不決，厭之，乃詔如舊，紓其征斂之期焉。

translations.literal: " The emperor, because the multitude of opinions were confused, over a month without decision, wearied of it, then edicted as before, easing the period for collection and levies.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month of fruitless debate the emperor tired of the wrangling and ordered that existing policy continue, only postponing the levy schedule.

sentences.zh: 未幾，竟用惠吉言，造「貞祐通寶」 。

translations.literal: Before long, they ultimately adopted Hui Ji's words and minted "Zhenyou Tongbao."
translations.idiomatic: Before long the court adopted Hui Ji's proposal and issued the "Zhenyou Tongbao" notes.

sentences.zh: 興定元年二月，始詔行之，凡一貫當千貫，增重偽造沮阻罪及捕獲之賞。

translations.literal: Xingding 1, second month, an edict first enforced it—every one string equals one thousand strings; increased weight of counterfeiting, obstruction, and reward for capture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Xingding 1 (1217) the new notes were formally issued, each one-string note redeemable for one thousand old strings, with heavier penalties for counterfeiting or obstructing circulation and rewards for informants.

sentences.zh: 五月，以鈔法屢變，隨出而隨壞，制紙之桑皮故紙皆取於民，至是又甚艱得，遂令計價，但征寶券、通寶、名曰「桑皮故紙錢」。

translations.literal: Fifth month, because the note law changed repeatedly, issued and immediately ruined, paper for manufacture—mulberry-bark recycled paper—all taken from the people; by now extremely hard to obtain—therefore ordered valuation, merely levying precious certificates and tongbao, called "mulberry-bark recycled-paper cash."
translations.idiomatic: In May, as repeated note reforms had exhausted mulberry-bark scrap paper requisitioned from the people, the court ordered a cash levy called "mulberry-bark recycled-paper money" payable in precious certificates or tongbao at assessed prices.

sentences.zh: 謂可以免民輸挽之勞，而省工物之費也。

translations.literal: They said it could spare the people transport and hauling labor and save labor and material costs.
translations.idiomatic: Officials claimed this would spare the people transport duties and save the state material costs.

sentences.zh: 高汝礪言：「河南調發繁重，所征租稅三倍於舊，僅可供億，如此其重也。

translations.literal: Gao Ruli said: "Henan's requisitions and dispatches are heavy and numerous—the rent and tax levied three times the old, barely enough to supply needs—so heavy is it."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ruli protested that Henan's levies and requisitions had already tripled old rates and barely kept the state afloat.

sentences.zh: 而今年五月省部以歲收通寶不充所用，乃于民間斂桑皮故紙鈔七千萬貫以補之，又太甚矣！

translations.literal: Yet this year in May the Secretariat and Ministry, because annual intake of tongbao did not fill needs, then from the people collected mulberry-bark recycled-paper notes of seventy million strings to supplement—again far too extreme!
translations.idiomatic: Then in May the central ministries had collected seventy million strings in mulberry-bark notes from the populace because tongbao receipts fell short—a step too far.

sentences.zh: 而近又以通寶稍滯，又增兩倍。

translations.literal: And recently, because tongbao were somewhat stagnant, they again doubled it.
translations.idiomatic: When tongbao circulation slowed, they doubled the levy again.

sentences.zh: 河南人戶農居三之二，今年租稅征尚未足，而複令出此，民若不糶當納之租，則賣所食之粟，舍此將何得焉？

translations.literal: Henan households—farmers occupy two-thirds; this year's rent and tax levy not yet complete, yet again ordered to produce this; if the people do not sell grain for rent due, then sell the grain they eat—apart from this, how would they obtain it?
translations.idiomatic: Two-thirds of Henan households were farmers still struggling to pay this year's taxes; if they did not sell grain to meet rent they would have to sell their food stores—how else could they comply?

sentences.zh: 今所急而難得者芻糧也，出於民而有限。

translations.literal: Now what is urgent and hard to obtain is fodder and grain—from the people and limited.
translations.idiomatic: Fodder and grain, drawn from a finite peasant surplus, were what the state urgently needed and could not easily find.

sentences.zh: 可緩而易為者交鈔也，出於國而可變。

translations.literal: What may be deferred and easily done is exchange notes—from the state and changeable.
translations.idiomatic: Paper notes, which the state could issue at will, were the flexible instrument.

sentences.zh: 以國家之所自行者而強求之民，將若之何？

translations.literal: Using what the state itself can produce and forcibly demanding it from the people—what then?
translations.idiomatic: How could the court shift onto the people burdens it ought to bear itself?

sentences.zh: 向者大鈔滯則更為小鈔，小鈔弊則改為寶券，寶券不行則易為通寶，變制在我，尚何煩民哉！

translations.literal: Formerly when large notes stagnated they changed to small notes; when small notes failed they changed to precious certificates; when precious certificates would not circulate they swapped to tongbao—in changing systems the power is ours—why still trouble the people!
translations.idiomatic: When large notes stalled the court had switched to small notes, then precious certificates, then tongbao—monetary reform was the state's prerogative, so why keep burdening the people?

sentences.zh: 民既悉力以奉軍而不足，又計口、計稅、計物、計生殖之業而加征，若是其剝，彼不能給，則有亡而已矣！

translations.literal: The people already exhausted their strength to supply the army yet it is insufficient, again counting mouths, counting taxes, counting property, counting reproductive livelihoods to add levies—if stripped thus, they cannot provide, then fleeing is all that remains!
translations.idiomatic: The people already gave all they had for the army and still fell short; now levies taxed their persons, lands, goods, and very livelihood—if stripped so bare they could only flee.

sentences.zh: 民逃田穢，兵食不給，是軍儲鈔法兩廢矣。

translations.literal: People flee, fields grow weed-choked, army provisions not supplied—this is both army stores and note law doubly abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Flight would leave fields fallow and armies hungry, ruining both military supply and the note system.

sentences.zh: 臣非于鈔法不加意，非故與省部相違也。

translations.literal: Your subject is not inattentive to the note law, nor intentionally at odds with the Secretariat and Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: I am not indifferent to monetary policy nor deliberately opposing the central ministries.

sentences.zh: 但以鈔滯物貴之害輕，民去軍饑之害重爾。

translations.literal: Only that the harm of notes stagnant and goods dear is light; the harm of people fleeing and army famine is heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Stagnant notes and rising prices were lesser evils than mass flight and army starvation.

sentences.zh: 」時不能用。

translations.literal: " At the time they could not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not act on his advice.

sentences.zh: 三年十月，省臣奏：「向以物重錢輕，犯贓者計錢論罪則太重，於是以銀為則，每兩為錢二貫，有犯通寶之贓者直以通寶論，如因軍興調發，受通寶及三十貫者，已得死刑，准以金銀價，才為錢四百有奇，則當杖。

translations.literal: Third year, tenth month, provincial ministers memorialized: "Previously because goods were heavy and cash light, judging bribery by cash count for punishment was too severe—therefore taking silver as standard, each tael equals two thousand cash; one who commits bribery in tongbao judged directly by tongbao—if due to military campaign requisitions, receiving tongbao reaching thirty strings, already deserving death penalty; converted at gold and silver price, only about four hundred-odd cash—then deserving cudgeling."
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of year three provincial officials reported that because goods were dear and cash cheap, valuing bribes in coin had made punishments absurd: thirty strings of tongbao carried the death penalty under military requisition law, yet at silver rates that was worth only about four hundred cash—barely warranting a beating.

sentences.zh: 輕重之間懸絕如此。

translations.literal: Between light and heavy the gap was so vast.
translations.idiomatic: The disparity between penalties was outrageous.

sentences.zh: 」遂命准犯時銀價論罪。

translations.literal: " An order followed to judge guilt according to silver price at time of offense.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered that bribery be assessed at prevailing silver rates.

sentences.zh: 四年三月，參知政事李複亨言：「近制，犯通寶之贓者並以物價折銀定罪，每兩為錢二貫，而法當贖銅者，止納通寶見錢，亦乞令依上輸銀，既足以懲惡，又有補於官。

translations.literal: Fourth year, third month, Vice Grand Councilor Li Fuheng said: "Recent regulation—those committing bribery in tongbao all convert goods' price to silver for guilt judgment, each tael two thousand cash; yet those under law who should redeem with copper cash only pay tongbao ready cash—I also petition to order them likewise to submit silver—both sufficient to punish evil and beneficial to the government."
translations.idiomatic: In March of year four Vice Grand Councilor Li Fuheng noted that while bribes in tongbao were now converted to silver at two thousand cash per tael, offenders who could commute punishment still paid in paper instead of silver; he asked that they pay silver too, both to deter crime and replenish the treasury.

sentences.zh: 」詔省臣議，遂命犯公錯過誤者止征通寶見錢，贓汙故犯者輸銀。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered provincial ministers to debate; then ordered that those who commit public errors through mistake only pay tongbao ready cash; those who commit filthy bribery through deliberate offense submit silver.
translations.idiomatic: After consultation the court ruled that petty official errors could be redeemed in tongbao cash, but deliberate corruption required silver payment.

sentences.zh: 十二月，鎮南軍節度使溫蒂罕思敬上書言：「錢之為泉也，貴流通而不可塞，積於官而不散則病民，散於民而不斂則闕用，必多寡輕重與物相權而後可。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, Zhennan Army military commissioner Wanyan Sijing memorialized: "Cash as a spring—precious is circulation and cannot be blocked; hoarded in government and not dispersed then harms the people; dispersed among the people and not collected then lacks for use—must have quantity, weight, light and heavy balanced against goods before it can work."
translations.idiomatic: In December Zhennan Army military commissioner Wanyan Sijing wrote that money, like a spring, must flow freely: hoarded in treasuries it oppressed the people, scattered unchecked it left the state short; only when quantity and value matched goods could it function.

sentences.zh: 大定之世，民間錢多而鈔少，故貴而易行。

translations.literal: In the Dading era, among the people cash was plentiful and notes few—therefore dear and easy to circulate.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizong coin had been plentiful and notes scarce, so cash held its value and circulated easily.

sentences.zh: 軍興以來，在官殊少，民亦無幾，軍旅調度悉仰于鈔，日之所出動以萬計，至於填委市肆，能無輕乎？

translations.literal: Since military campaigns began, in government extraordinarily little, among the people also almost none; army travel and supply all rely on notes—daily outflow constantly in the ten-thousands; as for filling and piling up in market shops—how could they not be light?
translations.idiomatic: Since the wars began official and private coin had dwindled while army logistics depended entirely on notes poured out by the ten thousands daily until markets overflowed—is it any wonder they collapsed in value?

sentences.zh: 不若馳限錢之禁 ，許民自采銅鑄錢，而官制模範，薄惡不如法者令民不得用，則錢必日多，鈔可少出，少出則貴而易行矣。

translations.literal: Better to lift the ban on cash limits, permit the people to mine copper and cast cash themselves, while the government sets the model; thin and inferior not conforming to law—order the people not to use—then cash will daily increase, notes can be issued less, less issuance then dear and easy to circulate.
translations.idiomatic: Better to end the cash monopoly, let people mine copper and cast coin to government specifications, and ban substandard coin; supply would grow, note printing could shrink, and notes would regain value.

sentences.zh: 今日出益眾，民日益輕，有司欲重之而不得其法，至乃計官吏之俸、驗百姓之物力以斂之，而卒不能增重，曾不知錢少之弊也。

translations.literal: Today issuance ever more numerous, among the people ever more devalued; responsible offices wishing to restore weight cannot find the method—even to calculating officials' salaries, testing common people's property strength to levy—yet ultimately cannot increase weight, never knowing the abuse of scarce cash.
translations.idiomatic: Today ever more notes drove ever greater devaluation; officials seeking to restore their value even taxed officials' salaries and assessed household wealth, yet failed because they ignored the root problem—too little coin.

sentences.zh: 臣謂宜令民鑄錢，而當斂鈔者亦聽輸銀，民因以銀鑄錢為數等，文曰「興定元寶」，定直以備軍賞，亦救弊之一法也。

translations.literal: Your subject says it is appropriate to order the people to cast cash; and where notes should be collected, also permit submitting silver—the people thus use silver to cast cash in several denominations, inscribed "Xingding Yuanbao," fixed value to supply military rewards—also one method of remedying abuses.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed private coinage with silver accepted in lieu of note levies, new "Xingding Yuanbao" coin in several denominations at fixed values for military pay—another stopgap reform.

sentences.zh: 」朝廷不從。

translations.literal: " The court did not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: The court rejected the proposal.

sentences.zh: 五年閏十二月，宰臣奏：「向者寶券既弊，乃造'貞祐通寶'以救之，迄今五年，其弊又複如寶券之末。

translations.literal: Fifth year, intercalary twelfth month, chief ministers memorialized: "Previously when precious certificates had failed, then minted 'Zhenyou Tongbao' to remedy—now five years to date—its abuses again match the end of precious certificates."
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary twelfth month of year five the chief ministers reported that the "Zhenyou Tongbao" issued five years earlier to replace failed precious certificates had now deteriorated to the same degree.

sentences.zh: 初，通寶四貫為銀一兩，今八百餘貫矣。

translations.literal: At first, four strings of tongbao equaled one tael of silver—now over eight hundred strings.
translations.idiomatic: Tongbao had initially traded at four strings per tael of silver; by now it took over eight hundred.

sentences.zh: 宜複更造'興定寶泉'，子母相權，與通寶兼行，每貫當通寶四百貫，以二貫為銀一兩，隨處置庫，許人以通寶易之。

translations.literal: Appropriate to again remint 'Xingding Baoquan,' parent and child mutually balanced, circulating together with tongbao—each string equals four hundred strings of tongbao, two strings equals one tael of silver; treasury established wherever, permitting people to exchange tongbao for them.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed new "Xingding Baoquan" notes in parent and child denominations to circulate alongside tongbao, each new string worth four hundred tongbao or half a tael of silver, with exchange treasuries where people could swap old notes.

sentences.zh: 縣官能使民流通者，進官一階、升職一等，其或姑息以致壅滯，則亦追降的決為差。

translations.literal: District officials who can make the people circulate them—advance rank one step, promote office one grade; if through indulgence causing stagnation—then also demoted rank with beatings as penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates who kept notes circulating would be promoted; those whose lax enforcement let them stagnate would be demoted and beaten.

sentences.zh: 州府官以所屬司縣定罪賞，命監察御史及諸路行部官察之，定撓法失糾舉法，失舉則御史降決，行部官降罰，集眾妄議難行者徒二年，告捕者賞錢三百貫。

translations.literal: Prefecture and district officials judged by their subordinate departments and counties for punishment and reward; ordered investigating censors and circuit inspection officials to supervise; fixed obstructions to law and failure to report violations—failure to report then censor demoted with beating, inspection official reduced penalty; gathering crowds to recklessly debate what is hard to execute—two years forced labor; informants rewarded three hundred strings cash.
translations.idiomatic: Prefecture officials would be judged by their counties' performance; censors and circuit inspectors would patrol and punish obstruction or failure to report violations; organizing resistance carried two years' penal servitude; informants received three hundred strings.

sentences.zh: 」元光元年二月，始詔行之。

translations.literal: " Yuanguang 1, second month, an edict first enforced it.
translations.idiomatic: The new system took effect in the second month of Yuanguang 1 (1222).

sentences.zh: 二年五月，更造每貫當通寶五十，又以綾印製「元光珍貨」，同銀鈔及餘鈔行之。

translations.literal: Second year, fifth month, reminted so each string equals fifty strings of tongbao; also used silk to print "Yuanguang Zhenhuo," circulating together with silver notes and remaining notes.
translations.idiomatic: In May of Yuanguang 2 the exchange rate was revised to fifty tongbao per new string; silk-printed "Yuanguang Zhenhuo" notes were also issued alongside silver and older notes.

sentences.zh: 行之未久，銀價日貴，寶泉日賤，民但以銀論價。

translations.literal: Not long enforced, silver price daily dearer, baoquan daily cheaper—the people only price by silver.
translations.idiomatic: Before long silver rose daily while Baoquan fell, and the market priced everything in silver alone.

sentences.zh: 至元光二年，寶泉幾於不用，乃定法，銀一兩不得過寶泉三百貫，凡物可直銀三兩以下者不許用銀，以上者三分為率，一分用銀，二分用寶泉及珍貨、重寶。

translations.literal: By Yuanguang 2, baoquan nearly unused—then fixed law: one tael of silver cannot exceed three hundred strings of baoquan; all goods worth below three taels of silver—use of silver forbidden; above—three parts as rate, one part silver, two parts baoquan and zhenhuo, chongbao.
translations.idiomatic: By Yuanguang 2 Baoquan was nearly worthless, so the court capped exchange at three hundred Baoquan per tael of silver, banned silver for purchases under three taels, and required larger transactions to split one-third silver and two-thirds Baoquan or other notes.

sentences.zh: 京師及州郡置平准務，以寶泉銀相易，其私易及違法而能告者罪賞有差。

translations.literal: Capital and prefectures set up leveling offices, exchanging baoquan and silver; private exchange and violators who can report—punishment and reward differ by degree.
translations.idiomatic: Exchange offices were established in the capital and prefectures to swap Baoquan and silver, with graded penalties for private dealing and rewards for informants.

sentences.zh: 是令既下，市肆晝閉，商旅不行，朝廷患之，乃除市易用銀及銀寶泉私相易之法。

translations.literal: Once this order was issued, market shops closed by day, merchants and travelers did not travel—the court worried, then abolished the law on market trade using silver and silver-baoquan private mutual exchange.
translations.idiomatic: Markets shut during daylight and commerce halted, so the court repealed the restrictions on silver use and private exchange.

sentences.zh: 然上有限用之名，而下無從令之實，有司雖知，莫能制矣。

translations.literal: Yet above there was the name of limited use, below no reality of obeying commands; responsible offices though knowing, none could control it.
translations.idiomatic: On paper use of paper money was restricted, but in practice no one obeyed and officials could not enforce the rules.

sentences.zh: 義宗正大間，民間但以銀市易。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Yizong in the Zhengda era, among the people only silver was used for market exchange.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yizong during the Zhengda reign the public traded only in silver.

sentences.zh: 天興二年十月印「天興寶會」于蔡州，自一錢至四錢四等，同見銀流轉，不數月國亡。

translations.literal: Tianxing 2, tenth month, printed "Tianxing Baohui" at Caizhou—from one qian to four qian in four grades, circulating together with ready silver—not several months and the state perished.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Tianxing 2 (1233) the court at Caizhou printed "Tianxing Baohui" notes from one to four qian in four denominations to circulate like silver; within months the dynasty fell.
